# v4 decisions

Decisions that `v4/DESIGN.md` leaves open, contradicts itself on, or that the environment forces. Made by the M0
conductor (2026-10-12) with the brief's rule: the design's own default first, else the reviewers' majority in
`v4f/comparison.md`, else the simplest. Every row is **default taken, for Tomáš** unless its status says otherwise;
Tomáš overrides by adding a row (never edit a decided row). Milestone conductors append rows as they go (`D40+`).
Line numbers refer to `v4/DESIGN.md` at f1f2dbd. Sources: own reading (R), Opus consistency scan (S#), Opus census
scan (C#), environment probe (P).

## Blocker

| # | Decision | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **D0** | **Base commit.** The worktree's v3 code is at `2d3cf90` (2026-08-26). The design (L16) and the census cite `9312c8c` (2026-10-08), the tip of `origin/dan/fetch-collect-metadata-updates-and-exploratory-dashboard`, not an ancestor of HEAD. 27 non-test files (~8k LOC) exist only there: `stack/{provider_transport,scholarly_records,http,arxiv,oa_adapter,metadata_*,abstract_*,card_date*}.py`, `stack/conversion/{ladder,worker}.py`, `stack/collect/identity.py`, `workflows/fetch/{arxiv,metadata,abstract,history,card_dates}`; the two-tier screen, `drain_page`, the pure fetchcycle patch builders. Verified: `git merge-base HEAD 9312c8c` = 2d3cf90; `2d3cf90` is an ancestor of `9312c8c`. **Default taken:** M1 starts with `git merge --no-ff 9312c8c` into this branch (expected conflicts only in `.gitignore`, `README.md`, and root docs our branch moved to `docs/history/`), so the design's file:line citations hold and `git mv` keeps the mapping. Fallback if refused: `git archive 9312c8c` into the scratchpad as the copy source (no `git mv` history for those files). | D5 | **`acquire` scope and state.** Scope = design's L232 ∪ {`state = 'triaged' AND content IS NOT NULL AND content.members_digest = identity.members_digest`} (a pure re-point after a fields-only change), **∩ `state IN ('triaged','acquired') AND NOT retired`**. `identified` rows are out of scope (counted in the run record as `out_of_scope`), masked rows keep progress but are not fetched. `acquired` is cumulative over `triaged` (S8/S9 as written). A re-point with no content change still writes the row (flat block changed) with `blocks_written = ['content']`. | S#1, S#2, R |
| D6 | **Merge carry.** On a merge `gather` writes `content` on the survivor: union of `snapshots[]` and `roles[]` keyed `(source_id, content_role)`, pointer fields left for `acquire` (state `identified`). That run's `blocks_written` includes `content`; X15 is per-file and needs no exemption. | S#3 |

## Added after the plan reviews (Astra A#, critic K#)

| # | Decision | Source |
|---|---|---|
| D36 | **Ledger reservation.** Before every outbound LLM attempt (first call, retry, adjudication tier, fallback model) the client atomically reserves a conservative cost (prompt tokens + `max_tokens`, at that model's price) against both the store total ($20.00) and the stage's `budget.max_usd`, in `cache/llm-ledger.jsonl` under an `O_EXCL` lock; the reservation is reconciled with the real cost after the response; reservations left by a crashed run stay charged until `stack gc --finalise-dead` releases them. Two parallel runs cannot both pass the same balance check. | A#4 |
| D37 | **Triage before acquire, from M2.** Because D5 puts `identified` rows out of acquire's scope, `workflows/triage/main.py` and `stack/gate.py` land in M2 (T2.9) with `sql:` clauses and the decision table; `question:` clauses are evaluated by a pluggable asker that M2/M3 leave unset (every question `skipped[not_requested]`, so a row with no positive `sql:` clause is `skip` under arm 2 when all clauses are `sql:`). The LLM asker and arms 3-6 arrive in M4 (T4.2). The dev plan's gate is `sql:`-only until M4. The M3 entry gate is the explicit integration run gather → triage → acquire → acquire (a four-file chain). | A#1, A#8 |
| D38 | **Locks and lost tails.** The chain lock `data/<chain>.lock` holds `{run_id, pid, heartbeat_at}`; a lock whose run is dead (D16) is breakable by `stack chain unlock <chain>` only; publish order is: write staged files → claim_base under the lock → rename files → write the final run record → release the lock; a crash between rename and final record leaves a `data/` file whose run record is still `running`/dead, which X1 (`finished_files`, now run over **all** `ok` run records, not only a build's) and `stack status` report, and `stack chain orphan` removes. | A#2 |
| D39 | **Convert dev pin.** Dev plans pin `pymupdf4llm` (tier 2) from the start of M3; docling (tier 1) is qualified in its own sub-task on three representative PDFs under the RLIMIT child's actual memory/time limits before any plan pins it; the import timing of the probe proves nothing about inference. | A#3 |
| D40 | **Retire order** (amended K#1). T1.8 retires `db/`, the DB-bound tests, `py-pglite`, `types/aggregates.py`, `workflows/aggregate/`, `v1_import`, the dead docling duplicates and the Postgres-only tools; **`psycopg` moves to the `dev` group** so v3's writer, `llm.py`, `read.py`, `inband.py` and the collectors stay importable as the ADAPT baseline. `core/{writer,db}.py`, `collect/identity.py`, `runner.py`, `configs/workflows.yaml` and `psycopg` go at T4.5. T1.8's Done: no v4 module imports `psycopg`, `core.writer`, `core.db` or `read`. | A#1, A#8, K#1 |
| D41 | **Runner name.** The v4 runner is `stack/stage_runner.py` until T4.5 (31 v3 sites import `stack.runner` for `Services`, `RunCounts`, `HaltRequested`); at T4.5 v3's `runner.py` is removed and `stage_runner.py` is `git mv`'d to `runner.py`. `stack/cli.py` → `stack/cli/__init__.py` at T1.3 (nothing in v3 imports `stack.cli`). | K#2 |
| D42 | **`workflows.yaml`.** Kept read-only for v3 modules until T4.5, then retired: stage registration, `bump_on` and scopes live in the plan files; `WorkflowReg.scope` SQL is dropped in T1.3c. `stack/config.py` is ADAPTed in T1.3c (`ChannelDef` loses `extra="forbid"` for the D13/D22 keys), not in T4.1. | K#3 |
| D43 | **Types frozen in T1.1.** Every A.2-A.5 pyarrow type, including `TRIAGE`, `SCREEN`, `AFFILIATION`, `DOC_CLASS`, is defined in T1.1; a later change is a schema bump (new `schema_digest`) that forces a full file and a `fold.compact` rewrite of `store-dev`, recorded in `RUNLOG.md`. | K#6 |
| D44 | **Ledger location.** `v4/llm-ledger.jsonl` (gitignored), outside the store; `gc` never touches it; `stack status --ledger` reads it. Amends D36. | K#12 |

| D46 | **Synthetic row factories.** `tests/synth/rows.py` (T1.1) holds minimal valid row factories per family (and a `tests/synth/__init__.py`); `tests/synth/world.py` (T1.7) builds the v4e world on top of them. | D48 | **`<wf>` and evidence column layout.** `<wf>`: SEL, then ANN common fields, then payload fields (exploded per item at item grain), then T2; a repeated name keeps its first occurrence (`evidence_id` from SEL, `status`/`error_class` from ANN, one `run_id`). Evidence: EVI, then the payload's top-level fields, then T2. `<wf>` and `corpus` files are chains of one (D14). | T1.1 builder, accepted |
| D49 | **`schema_digest`** = sha256 of canonical JSON (`jcs`) of `[[name, type, nullable], …]` over the schema; lists render `{"list":[item, item_nullable]}` (item name ignored), structs `{"struct":[…]}`, other types `str(type)`; key-value metadata excluded. | T1.1 builder, accepted |
| D50 | **`ids_digest`** = sha256 of the sorted key values joined by `\n`; composite keys joined by `\x1f` first; timestamps rendered `%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%fZ`. Refines D19. | T1.1 builder, accepted |
| D51 | **S6 id formats** follow `stack/core/ids.py` (type letter + 12 Crockford = 13 chars): `source_id`/`doc_id` `s…`, `run_id` `r…`, `evidence_id` any letter, `snapshot_id = <run_id>.<n>`, `file_id = <run_id>.<family>`, `*_digest` 64-hex; no column is a 16-hex derived id. §2.2's 10-char example `8k3m2p1q4r` is illustrative only. | T1.1 builder, accepted |
| D52 | **Block nullability and struct order.** `identity`, `metadata`, `inband`, `annotations` non-null, `content` nullable (D7); `ROLE.lane` last in `ROLE`; `SNAPSHOT.text_error_class` right after `text_status`. `stack/schemas/structs.py` added (breaks the blocks↔payloads import cycle). Affiliation `text_bearing = [items[].author_surface, items[].affiliations[].surface]` (builder's reading; design names only screen's). S5 "evidence unique" read as triage questions unique per row. | T1.1 builder, accepted |
| D53 | **Header.** Every file carries all 27 A.6 keys as strings; non-fold files hold `'none'` for the four fold keys; `stage ∈ {gather, triage, acquire}` ⇒ `blocks_written` is a JSON list, otherwise `'*'`. File-name stamp `YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ` (§2.2's example). The in-memory S3 fake lives in `tests/test_store_parquet.py`, not in `backend.py`. | T1.1 builder, accepted |
| D54 | **`chain_id` naming.** `documents` chain: `documents`. `sources`/`coverage`: one chain per collector stage, `sources.<channel>` / `coverage.<channel>` (the writer's channel, e.g. `sources.arxiv`); D17's build-record keys follow. Chains of one (`corpus`, `<wf>`, `<wf>_evidence`): `chain_id = file_id` (D14). | M1 conductor, R |
| D55 | **`stack/runs.py` is started by T1.2**, not T1.3: the A.7 run-record dataclass, D16 final-record path and zstd-JSON writer/reader, and `files_without_ok_record(store)` (the X1-over-run-records basis T1.2's lost-tail test needs). T1.3 extends it with provisional records, heartbeat and dead-run derivation. Sequential tasks, so no write conflict. | M1 conductor, R |
| D56 | **Channel config keys** (T1.3c). `ChannelDef` gains `channel_group` (required; `paper`: openalex, arxiv, europepmc, semantic_scholar; `forum`: lesswrong, alignmentforum; `url`: every blog, every `*_cards`, `manual`), `miss_means = 'unknown'`, `non_merging_keys = []`, `record_projection = []`; `extra="forbid"` stays (the new keys are explicit fields). `ChannelsConfig.channel_groups` maps each group to its merging key kinds (§6); non-merging kinds `related, relay, conversation_id, reply_to_id, quote_of, repost_of`; `url`/`record` merge on `url`/`registry_id`. `vocab.py` gains `CHANNEL_GROUPS`. `configs/channels.yaml` 1.6.0, `configs/workflows.yaml` 3.0.0 (14 `scope:` blocks and `&fetch_gate` removed, D42). | T1.3c builder, accepted |
| D57 | **v3 scope readers.** `config.V3_SCOPED_WORKFLOWS` (frozen list of the 14 workflows that had a `scope`) replaces the dropped `WorkflowReg.scope` at v3 call sites (`stack/runner.py`, `stack/core/writer.py`, `tools/{dashboard_fetch_sql,check_scope_live}.py`); v3's runner refuses those steps with `ScopeError`. Keeps every v3 module importable until T4.5; the DB-bound tests that used `scope` (`test_runner_e2e`, `test_receipts`, `test_dashboard_acquisition`) retire at T1.8/T4.5. | T1.3c builder, accepted |
| D58 | **`spec/schemas/config/*.schema.json` are maintained with the configs**: `tools/check_configs.py` validates against them, so a config key change edits the schema too (outside PLAN §0's write list; allowed for this reason). | M1 conductor, R |
| D59 | **`read_view` row selection.** The §7.3 window runs in duckdb over `(pos, file_row_number)` only; the winning rows are then taken from the parquet files by pyarrow, so the view is byte-identical to what was written (a duckdb round trip of the rows nulled non-nullable children of a NULL `content`, which the writer refuses). | T1.2 builder, accepted |
| D60 | **Stale-lock rule.** A lock is stale when: same host and the pid is gone (even if the run has an `ok` record, so a crash after the final record is recoverable); or the run is `running` with `heartbeat_at` older than the timeout (default 5 min until the plan's `recovery.heartbeat_timeout` is wired in T1.3); or the pid cannot be checked / the record is final and the lock's heartbeat is old; an unreadable lock is held while its mtime is fresh, else stale. A held lock is never broken; `unlock` without `force` raises on a stale lock (the CLI needs `--force`). Lock JSON carries `host` too. Several heads with no shared base raise `ForkError`. Amends D38. | T1.2 builder, accepted |

| D89 | **`gc` keeps every chain resolvable** (amends D79's `superseded` rule). gc deletes a chained-family `data/` file only if it lies in the **strict prefix of the head's ancestry older than every kept anchor**. Ancestry = the head's walk back over *all* base pointers, stopping at base `none` or a base not in `data/`. Anchors = the view's first file (the newest full) and, per file a build record names (any status, as D79), that file's nearest full ancestor (the walk's oldest file if none), so a build's own view stays readable. Kept = anchor to head; candidates = everything older, by segment (a full file and its parts) aged from the next full file's `finished_at`, the prefix ending at the first segment younger than `--older-than` (the kept set stays a suffix). The oldest kept file is therefore a full file (its dangling base is never walked) and no kept file loses its successor (no second head, the gate's `ForkError`). Chains of one: never (D79); staged and orphaned categories unchanged. Tombstones also carry `file_id`. Base-view checks (V12, X15, X17, X22, X24, D76): a file whose base walk meets a tombstoned file is not checkable; with no other finding the check reports `skipped[base_collected]` (whole check, `SkipCheck`: the result has no per-pair status), with findings it fails as before. No other test exceeds ~5 s (serial `--durations=40`, longest outside the two modules 2.11 s), so nothing else is marked. Timings (2026-10-12): fast `-m "not slow"` `-n auto` 1127 passed, 5 skipped in 26.05 s, serial 105.18 s; full `-n auto` 1142 passed, 5 skipped in 34.38 s, serial 121.73 s; `-m slow` 15 passed in 8.64 s (`-n auto`), 19.92 s serial; 1127 + 15 = 1142. Policy in PLAN §0 `[T#1]`. | Tomáš 2026-10-12 (via conductor), T1.8-s |

| D185 (C) | **Strict structured-output schemas; served-provider names mapped to egress slugs (M4 real part; `stack/llm/__init__.py`, `workflows/annotate/screen/main.py`; default taken, for Tomáš).** Real screen run `rjcc50mywvd3z` (luna): every `first` attempt answered 400 on the strict `response_format`, every call re-sent degraded (2 round trips, nothing enforced by the provider); triage's closed, all-required schema was accepted (`rxvbysx065a6m`). (1) One shared rule, not per-workflow schemas: `stack.llm.strict_schema` (pure, idempotent): every object closed and listing all its properties in `required`; an optional property becomes nullable (scalar: `type` gains `"null"`, an `enum` gains `null`; object/array/untyped: `anyOf [it, {type: null}]`); a string `enum` without `type` gets `type: string`; annotation keywords (`$schema`, `$id`, `title`, `x-*`, `$defs`) dropped; a `$ref` raises (inline first). Chosen over hand-written per-workflow schemas because affiliation (phase 2) needs the same rule on nested objects, and triage's schema is already a fixed point. (2) `stack.llm.wire_schema`, applied by the client to EVERY `response_format`: only `type, properties, required, additionalProperties, enum, items, anyOf, description, minimum, maximum` go on the wire (`minimum`/`maximum` because triage sends them and is accepted); everything else (`maxLength`, `minItems`, `pattern`, …) stays client-side (`validate_json` checks the full schema; screen's 400/200-char caps still refuse). This changes the wire for any other workflow whose schema carries other keywords (loosens provider enforcement only; digests unchanged: they hash the schema passed, not the wire form). (3) `stack.llm.fill_nulls`: before validation the client sets an absent property whose schema admits `null` to `None` (recursively), so a degraded reply (fallback kept for providers that still refuse) that omits an optional key reads it `null` instead of a schema-invalid retry; under strict mode it is a no-op. (4) Screen: `SCHEMA = strict_schema(_output_schema(...))`; `quotes`, `buckets`, `off_topic_reason`, `grounding_idx` required-nullable (screen.md "optional", screen-v8's conditional quote rule cannot be expressed in strict mode and stays a prompt rule); `_payload` already read `null` as absent (`or []`). `_output_schema` keeps returning the optional-key form because v3's `tools/eval_screen.py` (and `tests/test_eval_screen.py`) validate with null keys dropped. **The screen template digests change (the schema is in `template_hash`), so every screen work key changes**: a `--prior` carry does not reuse pre-D185 screen rows. (5) `_served_provider_slug`: display name → slug table `PROVIDER_SLUGS` (Google → google-vertex, Google AI Studio → google-ai-studio, OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepInfra, Amazon Bedrock, Azure, plus OpenInference → open-inference, InferenceNet → inference-net, AtlasCloud → atlas-cloud from track E's keyless `/endpoints` reads, case-insensitive); any other name keeps today's derived slug (lowercase, hyphenated), so an unknown provider outside the sanctioned set stays an anomaly (loud), a missing field stays "cannot tell". (b) `relist_after_h` (option, default 12 h): a listing surface (feeds, sitemaps, scrape and card pages) read `ok` within it is skipped; a partial window truncated by a fixed cap is skipped within it as well (asking again returns the identical truncation; **deviation from the brief**, which said partial windows are retried), except in blogs and cards, where the cap is on new sources so a retry progresses and a partial surface stays due. | D235 (ANN) | **Annotate inputs: chained annotators and a scope over annotation records (round 5, T-ANN 1; review R1-6, R5-5 (4); Tomáš 2026-10-13 "Port all of the 4 … in the background"; semantics default taken, for Tomáš; shared core `stack/{plan,build}.py`, `stack/annotate/*`, `stack/fold/__init__.py`, `stack/schemas/{vocab.py,payloads/registry.py}`, `stack/checks/annotate.py`).** DESIGN §3.1 already lists "named `<wf>` files" as `annotate.<wf>` inputs; this makes them real. (1) **Two kinds of reads.** *Basis reads*: registry `PayloadSpec.reads` names the annotations (workflows or records) whose selected result the workflow's ask consumes (model_roles reads model_mentions); such a workflow has the new basis kind **`chained`**: `basis_digest = H([current_text_digest, [[name, H([status, payload])] for each read]])`, over the read's typed `ANN` after mapping M, so an upstream change re-asks the dependent and an upstream re-run with the same result carries it; no text → `skipped[no_text]`, a read not `ok`/`empty` → `skipped[no_basis]`. *Scope reads*: a plan stage line's `reads: [<name>…]` joins annotations for the `filter:` only (e.g. `reads: [stack_relevance]`, `filter: "ann_verdict(annotations, 'stack_relevance') = 'relevant'"`); they are **not** in the basis: a scope input decides whether a document is annotated, not what the answer depends on, so a screen re-run that keeps a document in scope re-asks nothing. (2) **Order.** A registry `reads` names an earlier registry entry (registry order is then a topological order). The plan loader orders stage lines stably by the edges `annotate.<producer of each read>` → reader (listed order kept otherwise; the validated plan, and so `plan_digest`, holds the resolved order); a cycle, or a read whose producer has no `annotate.<producer>` line, is a `PlanError`; `fold.build.annotations_folded` naming a `chained` workflow must fold its basis reads too (else every row would map stale). A read the producer's pin does not produce is refused at build start like a folded record (`refuse_unproduced_records`, `missing_input`). (3) **Build and stage.** `stage_inputs` passes `corpus` plus `<name>` = this build's file for every read (basis ∪ line); one missing fails the build `missing_input`. `run_annotate` refuses any other input and any missing read, joins the reads into the corpus rows in memory with `stack.fold.join` (mapping M included), then applies the scope filter; `AskItem.row["annotations"][<read>]` is what the ask sees. (4) **Mapping M, X7, X8.** One function computes the `chained` current basis from a row's `annotations` block; `fold.join` applies it in a second pass after the non-chained annotations, in registry order; `select`, X7 and X8 call it on the corpus rows joined from the run header's `inputs` (the checks rebuild the joined corpus the stage saw). | T-ANN conductor |

Observation history beyond the newest non-miss row is still compacted away; the head carries the counts (D261). | D258 (RUN) | **Run liveness and writer locks: a heartbeat error never discards a run, a live run is never finalised dead, overlapping writers are refused at start (round 5, T-RUN item 3; R6-1, R6-3, R2-2, R2-3, R2-5, R2-7, R2-8, R2-9, R2-10; default taken, for Tomáš).** (1) The heartbeat logs a failed save and retries; it gives up only after failures last longer than half the plan's `heartbeat_timeout`; a stop error becomes a warning and the run still stages and publishes; the heartbeat runs until publish returns. If gc nevertheless wrote `failed[crashed]` for a run that was alive, the run replaces that record with its real outcome at its end (outputs stay published); any other existing final record is kept and the run's own goes beside it as `<name>.conflict-<hex>.json.zst`. Once a final record exists, no handler rewrites it and publish does not roll back. (3) Writer intent: before dispatch a run declares its writes (`stack.build.stage_writes`, or a stage module's `WRITES`; stages outside the known phases, `echo_test` and `migrate.*`, count as writing every chained chain they pinned) under an `O_EXCL` `runs/.start.lock`, and refuses `failed[writer_running]` when a live run declares an overlapping write; a held or stale chain lock is refused before the stage runs (R2-3). Collectors on different channels and screen ∥ affiliation stay allowed. (4) `runs/builds/.<plan>.lock`: a second build of the same plan writes `failed[build_running]` and runs nothing (R2-10). (6) gc skips chains with an unrecorded view file (R2-2); `chain orphan` refuses a recorded middle file without `--force` (R2-9); run records keep unknown keys and warn (R2-5). Open: pid reuse is not detected; `stack fold`/`migrate` use the 10-minute default timeout. Commit `407768b`. | B3 (RUN) |

| D281 (SCALE) | **Incremental verify: what a build's "verified" means (round 5, T-SCALE; R2-6's second fix).** The pair checks are V12, X13, X15, X17, X19, X22 and X24: a chain file against its base view. Each build record's `verify.pairs` holds `version` (`PAIR_CHECKS_VERSION`, now 1), `reference`, `mode`, `files` (check → the file ids that passed it) and the `checked`/`inherited` counts. `stack verify` and the build's verify step skip, per pair check, the files that the reference lists for that check. The reference is the newest build record (`ok` or `incomplete`) whose verify passed under the same version; with `--build`, it is that build. Everything else runs in full on every verify: the file-scope checks, X1 over all records and `data/`, X4, X5, X9, X14, X20, and so on. `stack verify --full` and `stack build --verify-full` re-check every file, with the same output item for item; a store with no such record is verified in full. **An `ok` build's "verified" means:** every check passed on the build's set, and each pair check passed on each retained chain file either in this build or in an earlier verified build that lists the file, under the same `PAIR_CHECKS_VERSION`. X1 pins the bytes of every `data/` file on every verify. Limits: (a) a fix to a pair check's code must bump `PAIR_CHECKS_VERSION`, or old files are not re-checked; (b) V12's reading of the `migrate.restate` part on a compaction is trusted from the time it was checked; (c) if a listed file's bytes change, X1 reports it, not the pair check; (d) if gc later deletes a listed file's base, the check reports `ok`, not `skipped[base_collected]`; (e) a file a check passes without comparing anything (X15 on `*` writers, X13 on non-acquire parts, empty files) is not recorded and runs again, which is cheap. Measured at 50k with six new files, one of them a 50k-row compaction: incremental 704 s against full 689 s, 573 s against 635 s CPU, the same peak. After D280 the pair checks are about 38 % of a full verify and the file-scope loop about 51 % (per-check attribution at 50k), so a build's verify time is now set mainly by the file-scope loop over all retained files. | D289 (R6) | **The OA lane runs in `fetch_workers - 2` slots grouped by DOI, with every request still one-at-a-time per host (T-R6 item 3; REH "Recorded, not attempted" 2: 815 OA calls on one slot over the 49-min fetch window, backfill projected 40-60 h).** Mechanism: `OaLane.host_key` (`workflows/acquire/lanes/oa.py` "Slots") puts a call in fetch group `oa:<k>`, `k` = CRC-32 of the member's identifier (`Identifiers.raw` lowercased, DOI else PMID, else the source id) mod `slots(env)` = `max(1, fetch_workers - 2)` (one worker left for the arXiv slot, one for the http hosts; at `fetch_workers` 1-3 the lane is one slot, as before). One slot's calls run in row order, so a member's `full_text` and `xml` stay back to back on one retrieval, and members sharing a DOI share a slot, so the run's negatives (`OaState.negatives`) apply in the order one worker would. Politeness is per host, not per slot: `stack.oa_adapter.RequestGate.send` now holds the run pacer's per-host in-flight lock (`HostPacer.hold`, the lock `PoliteFetcher` already holds for the http/arXiv lanes) around pace + send + body read (a streamed body is read under the lock up to `max_bytes + 1` and replayed), so no host sees two requests from the process at once, whichever lane or slot sends them; under it stay the pacer's per-host rate (fetchpdf ladder `rate_limits` via `seed_rates`: Unpaywall 5 rps, Crossref 10, OpenAlex 5, S2 1, NCBI 3; else 1 rps), the cross-process `Gate` (per-family interval and slots; Crossref re-reads `x-rate-limit-limit`/`-interval` from responses), and fetchpdf's own token buckets. Alternative not taken: groups by DOI registrant prefix (publisher proxy): the hosts an OA call reaches are mostly the shared resolver APIs, which the per-host lock serialises anyway, and a large prefix (Zenodo's `10.5281` was 121 of 415 members here) would become one long group. Thread safety: `RequestGate.active` wraps `HTTPAdapter.send` once while any thread has a gate active (counted, restored by the last exit) and routes each call to the calling thread's gate (a thread without one goes straight through; before, the wrap was process-wide per block, which nested blocks in two threads would have torn down under each other); 429 records are per thread (`limited`/`take`), so one slot's 429 never classifies another member; `OaState.last` is per slot; the lane's own `requests.Session` is per thread; the session build is locked; each walk gets its own `mkdtemp` scratch directory; the run cache and negatives are plain dicts written whole (two slots may both ask the same URL once). fetchpdf's session, resolver, resolution cache and limiter are shared as fetchpdf's own batch mode shares them across its thread pool (`fetchpdf.py` `shared_resolver`, `_DaemonThreadPoolExecutor`; `retrieval/ratelimit.py` and `cache.py` lock-guarded); its retrieval starts no threads, so a member's requests stay on its thread. Unchanged: `halt_run` (a provider 429/cooldown stops admitting OA items; calls in flight finish and are applied), outcome application in row/role order, `budget.max_minutes`, the `fetch_workers = 1` loop. No plan option added (none needed; std-v3 keeps `fetch_workers: 8` → 6 OA slots), no plan digest changed. Rates used and their sources: Crossref "Access and authentication" page (read 2026-10-13, last updated 2025-10-16): polite pool 10 requests (`x-rate-limit-limit`/`-interval`), concurrency 3 (`x-concurrency-limit`); we send at most one at a time. Zenodo developers page (read 2026-10-13): guests 60 requests/min and 2,000/hour; the `Gate`'s 2.1 s Zenodo interval (≈ 1,714/h) is under the hourly cap. Unpaywall: its API page renders only with JavaScript and was not read; the 5 rps is fetchpdf's ladder value and the mandatory `email` is sent as before; its daily volume limit is **unverified** here. Measured (RUNLOG (R6-OA), same 726 due OA roles on two reflink copies of store-reh-7d, std-v3 minus `archive`, `--only fetch`): before 250 OA calls in 629 s = 23.8 calls/min (halted by one Semantic Scholar 429 at 555 s); after 721 calls in 990 s = 43.7 calls/min, scope complete, no halt (×1.84); requests 62.8 → 108.5/min; every host's peak in flight 1 in both runs (overall peak 5, mean 1.2); `zenodo.org` busy 85 % of the after run (389 requests: record, redirect, file), which bounds this mix. Outcomes on the 249 roles both runs charged: identical except 2 `rate_limit` → `ok` / `no_fetchable_url`; 429s 10 → 4, 403s on those roles 1 → 1, `no_fetchable_url` 196 → 197. Tests: `tests/test_acquire_fetch_workers.py` (slots overlap at a barrier, every host's peak in flight 1, rows/snapshot ids/counts equal to one worker on an 18-member world; one walk per member under 8 workers; provider 429 halts, the other slot's in-flight member is applied, nothing more of the halting slot is called; slot arithmetic), `tests/test_fetch_oa.py` (one gate in two threads + a gate-less thread; body read under the host lock); each seen red under a mutation (no `host_key`; no host lock; one shared `last`; the old `active`; no body read; shared 429 list). Default taken, for Tomáš: the slot count `fetch_workers - 2`. | T-R6 OA builder |

| D307 (BATCH) | **Batch mode: a stage line's `llm_mode: batch` (default `sync`) sends its LLM calls through OpenRouter's batch API at half price by collect, submit, replay; all of it lives in the one client of one run, nothing outlives the run but the response cache and the ledger (T-BATCH; Tomáš 2026-10-13: "Batch API: test and build it … Would switch to that from worker threads if we can"; clean architecture, no state shared between runs).** Mechanism: `stack/llm/batch.py` `prefetch(client, asks, options=…)` runs the stage's admitted items' **normal** ask code in collect passes, where `LlmClient.complete()` answers from the response cache or this run's batch outcomes and otherwise records the first request the call loop would send and raises `Deferred` (not an `LlmError`, so no workflow swallows it). Requests are reserved and submitted as they are collected, per `(model, provider slug)` chunk (`batch_max_requests` 2,000 / `batch_max_mb` 40; one model and one provider per batch); `POST /batches` with `endpoint, model, provider {only: [<egress slug>], allow_fallbacks: false}, requests [{custom_id, body}]`, body = the sync payload minus its `provider` block; polled at 15/30/60 s by age; each result settles through the call loop's own HTTP-200 code (refactored into `_inspect_200`/`_answer`: parse, strict-schema validation, egress backstop, usage, truncation; the same response-cache entry plus `via: batch`, `batch_id`). A pass whose answers admit further calls (screen's tier 2 after a borderline tier 1) is followed by another pass, up to 4. Then `client.batch_replay()` and the stage's **unchanged** sync loop runs as the replay pass: `answered` keys come from the cache with `is_cache_hit = false` and the batch attempt's cost and latency (submit to result), so the evidence rows are written by the sync code; a batch result that is not clean (parse error, schema-invalid, truncated, 5xx, `error` item, missing) is asked sync in the replay after the paid batch attempt (`retry_sync`; a truncated one at twice the cap); `ContextTooLarge` and auth errors are raised as in sync; a pass of fewer than `batch_min_requests` (100) requests is asked sync (`sync`). Wiring: `stack/annotate/batchmode.py` (option validation before any call, `run_batches`, counts), `run_annotate` (+36/−10: one item builder shared by prefetch and loop; `BatchUnanswered` → `not_attempted[unanswered]`), the triage asker (pairs of the first `max_rows` documents; `llm_mode` and `batch_*` kept out of the triage `config_digest`: every plan's digests unchanged). Every annotate workflow works unchanged (screen, affiliation, model_roles, technique_roles: read for broad `except`s; affiliation verified by test; model_mentions makes no call). Counts `batch.{passes, requests, batches, answered, retry_sync, sync, refused_budget, unanswered, fatal, error, batches_failed, batches_expired, batches_abandoned, submit_errors, wait_s, sync_fallback}`. `FakeLlm` is also a batch transport (every scripted reply works in batch mode). Tests `tests/test_llm_batch.py`, `tests/test_batch_stages.py` (triage, screen's two tiers and affiliation give the sync rows except ids, cost, latency; chunking, partial failures, expired/failed/never-finishing batches, ledger settle, cache across runs, budget stop, submit errors); each behaviour mutation-checked by its builder (lists in the builders' status files). Commits `79f42a3` (client), `b8cd03c` (vocab, build reason), `b82bcad` (stages), `bb41972` (fixes after an adversarial review). | conductor (BATCH), builders CORE, STAGES, FIX |
| D308 (BATCH) | **Money in batch mode: reserve at half price at submit, settle from the reported cost, and never record a possibly billed batch as $0; caps apply as in sync (T-BATCH).** (1) Each request is reserved right before its chunk is submitted (the client's formula × `BATCH_PRICE_FACTOR` 0.5: every `:batch` variant on OpenRouter's model list is half the sync price on every line, cache reads included, 2026-10-13). The stage's `budget.max_usd` and the ledger cap are enforced there: a refusal while other batches are in flight submits what is reserved, waits for them to settle (actuals free headroom) and retries; with nothing in flight it is the budget stop: every request not yet submitted is `refused`, the replay raises `BudgetExceeded` at the first such key and `BudgetScope` makes it and the rest `not_attempted[budget]`, as in sync. (2) Settle: a result's own `usage.cost`; batch-level `usage.cost` left over by per-result costs is shared over the calls without a costed result (tokens × price × 0.5, or the reserved amount where no tokens are known), so the ledger holds what the batch billed. (3) **There is no cancel** (`POST /batches/:id/cancel` 404, measured; DELETE only on terminal batches), so a batch the run gives up on is billed anyway: a batch still in flight at the time cap or when anything raises out of the passes (a code bug, Ctrl-C), and a submit whose response was lost to the network (never resent: a 40 MB POST can time out after the server accepted it), are reconciled at reserved × the run's actual/reserved ratio so far (1.0 before any settled), never released at $0; a submit is retried only after a 5xx or 429. Partial results of failed/expired batches are settled. A crashed process still leaves its open reservations to `stack gc --finalise-dead` (released): a known gap, the batch ids are printed on stderr for a manual check. | D390 (e2e-fix) | **Triage output cap 1,024 tokens through a new llm.yaml role `classify_1k`, not a raised `classify` (P1; Tomáš: "Raise the cap").** The triage cap is only its role's `max_tokens` (`workflows/triage/ask.py` `resolve`; the pin may carry `name, model, role, template_digest`). Users of `classify`: triage (default role), `collect.links` (role for the model only; its own `max_tokens` 12,000), `tests/fakes/annotate.py`, `evals/screen/2026-10-13-t2pool/scripts/dc_sep.py`, and the triage eval harness (`evals/triage/2026-10-12a`, role `classify`). Raising `classify` would change the triage `template_digest`, so `asker_name` and the triage `config_digest` of every plan on the default role (std-v2, std-v3, dev plans): every existing store re-asks all triage on its next build, and triage eval caches miss. A new role changes only plans that name it. llm.yaml 1.10.0: `classify_1k: {model: openai/gpt-6-luna, max_tokens: 1024}`; std-2026-10-14a pins `role: classify_1k`. Cause: gpt-6-luna used the whole 512 tokens on reasoning for 4.8% of rows (batch test). Open for Tomáš: make 1,024 the default for all triage (raise `classify`, accepting the re-triage), or a plan-level `max_tokens` in the triage pin as `collect.links` has. | builder e2e-fix |
| D391 (e2e-fix) | **Acquire `options.order` (`doc_id` or `newest_first`), and unknown acquire options refused (P2; Tomáš: "Ok" to newest first under the cap).** `workflows.acquire.scope.select(order=)`: `newest_first` sorts the scope by `metadata.published_at` descending, ties by `doc_id`, undated rows last (naive timestamps read as UTC); every substage walks the scope in that order, so `max_rows`/`budget.max_minutes` keep the newest rows; the part file stays in `doc_id` order. Default `doc_id` (unchanged). `check_options` refuses an unknown key (naming the closest known one), a bad `order`, a `max_rows`/`convert_max_rows` that is not an int >= 0 or null, a `convert_max_minutes` that is not a number > 0 or null: a `StageError` in `run` before any substage, and in acquire's `preflight`, so a build fails `stage_refused` at its start. `OPTIONS` lists the 19 keys the stage, its substages and lanes read; a test greps `workflows/acquire/` for read keys. Acquire only: option reading is per stage (no shared schema), so a general check needs every stage to declare its options: a review item. `max_rows` is now strict (it was `int(...)`, accepting strings and negatives). | builder e2e-fix |
| D392 (e2e-fix) | **Convert's own stops: `options.convert_max_rows` and `options.convert_max_minutes` (P3, P3b).** Before, `max_rows` also capped convert's rows and convert's clock was the stage's (`budget.max_minutes` from the stage start). In-band bodies (LW/AF/forum posts, raw HTML waiting for convert, D10) need no fetch but took convert's row quota, so with ~8k in-band posts in the e2e window the fetched PDFs stayed `convert_pending` and unscreened; and a fetch stopped by the budget left convert no time. Now `convert_max_rows` (int >= 0, null = no cap) caps convert; absent = `max_rows` (the old behaviour, kept for std-v3 and other plans). `convert_max_minutes` (number > 0) runs convert on its own clock from the start of convert; absent = the stage clock (old behaviour). A stage with both can run `budget.max_minutes` + `convert_max_minutes`. Open for Tomáš: whether the defaults should flip (convert uncapped by `max_rows`; convert always on its own clock) for std-v3's 90-min backfill runs, where the old defaults still starve convert. | builder e2e-fix |
| D400 (review) | **The client-wide LLM breaker is time-based as well as count-based (amends D146's breaker).** `LlmClient` trips `FatalLlmError` only when the failure streak has reached `_MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES` (25, unchanged) AND lasted at least `_MIN_FAILURE_STREAK_S` (120 s, new module constant; constructor `min_failure_streak_s`) since its first failure with no HTTP 200 in between; the streak start is kept under `_state_lock` with the count and cleared by a 200. Why: finding L5-1 (impl/25 review): the count was sized for v3's single worker; at `workers: 32` one round of in-flight calls failing in a ~1 s 429/5xx/network blip reached 25 and halted the whole run (every later row `not_attempted[halted]`; repro: 1 s 429 window, 32 workers, 200/200 fatal). Unchanged: 401/402/403 fatal at once; per-call `max_call_failures` (4) and the backoff. Test `tests/test_llm_breaker.py` (1 s window at 32 workers -> 200 ok, 0 fatal, red at 951aae4; endless 429 with a 0.3 s minimum -> trips; 32 failures inside the minimum -> no trip; 402 -> fatal at once); `test_transport_error_releases_its_reservation` pins `min_failure_streak_s=0.0` to keep its count-only trip. Open for Tomáš: the 120 s default, and whether a 429 storm should pause all workers (a shared backoff) instead of each call backing off alone. | builder review-fix |
| D402 (review) | **An S2 rate limit no longer halts the OA lane (amends D164 for S2).** `workflows/acquire/lanes/oa.py`: new `OPTIONAL_PROVIDER_HOSTS = {"api.semanticscholar.org"}`; `rate_limited` sets `halt_run` only when a provider/resolver limit comes from a host outside it (`any(x.provider and x.host not in OPTIONAL_PROVIDER_HOSTS ...)`). A role limited only by S2, by a 429 after the gate's retries or by a standing cross-process `Gate` cooldown (`stack/oa_adapter.py` records both as `Limited`, unchanged), is `failed_transient[rate_limit]`, charged as a content-host limit is, with the `Retry-After` hint, and the lane goes on. Why: finding L4-1 (impl/25 review): S2 is one optional source of fetchpdf's walk, not a resolver every paper needs; with S2 throttled (46 of 58 requests 429 in smoke A) the first OA paper whose walk reached S2 without a copy halted the OA lane for the run, every later OA role `not_attempted[halted]`. Unpaywall, the ID Converter and the other Gate families still halt. Tests (`tests/test_fetch_oa.py`, red before the fix): `test_an_s2_429_without_a_copy_does_not_halt_the_lane` (no halt, hint, the next paper still fetched), `test_a_standing_s2_cooldown_does_not_halt_the_lane_but_another_providers_does` (S2 cooldown no halt; OpenAlex alone or with S2 halts); `test_a_429_from_a_resolver_api_halts_the_run` unchanged. Open: `_fetch_parallel` counts admitted rows toward `max_rows` before any call, so halted rows hog the quota under `fetch_workers` (repro `test_l4_halt_quota.py`, not changed tonight); only `api.semanticscholar.org` is optional (another S2 host still halts). For Tomáš: whether S2 belongs in the OA walk while the key is throttled (default: keep it, never halting on it). | builder review-fix |
| D401 (review) | **A Gate cooldown no longer cascades into synthetic 429s in the collect transport (finding L3-1, impl/25 review).** One real 429 without retry-after sets the Gate's 60 s cooldown, during which `throttled_open` answers a synthetic 429 without sending; `Transport.request` counted each as `http_429` and halved the pacer, so one real S2 429 failed the page, left the pacer at the 0.05 rps floor for the run and ended `collect.s2-lookup` (`scope_complete=false`). Now (1) `throttled_open` marks the synthetic 429 with the header `X-Stack-Cooldown: 1` (`provider_transport.COOLDOWN_HEADER`); `Transport.request` counts it as `http_cooldown`, not as `http_requests`/`http_429`, and never penalizes for it; (2) `Transport.request` waits out a cooldown of at most `halt_429_after_s` (`COOLDOWN_WAIT_MAX_S` = 60 s when the pacing sets none, e.g. S2 collect) and re-sends, at most `COOLDOWN_WAITS` = 3 times per request; a longer cooldown halts the run when the pacing halts on 429 (as a real 429 asking that long does), else comes back as the 429. The wait uses the transport's injected sleep and re-checks `collector.halted` after it; the Transport has no stop/cancel hook, so it is not otherwise interruptible (<= 60 s). This covers every `Transport` user: the collectors (S2, OpenAlex, ...) and both lookups. (3) A real 429 on a gate-paced family (`provider_transport.gate_interval`, factored out of `Gate.interval`) halves the pacer no lower than the Gate's interval (`HostPacer.penalize(host, floor_rps=...)`; a rate already below is kept); other hosts halve to 0.05 rps as before. Acquire's fetchpdf: unchanged and fail-fast; `oa_adapter` catches `Cooldown` from its own Gate dispatch and `attach_requests_gate` is untouched, so the cooldown wait is opt-in by going through `Transport`; acquire's urllib lanes see one extra header on the synthetic 429 and nothing else (their `PoliteFetcher` still penalizes a synthetic 429, left as is: same class of bug, acquire-owned, not changed tonight). Tests `tests/test_collect_cooldown.py`: `test_s2_collect_one_real_429_waits_out_the_cooldown`, `test_s2_lookup_one_real_429_keeps_the_batch`, `test_lookup_429_asking_above_halt_threshold_still_halts[real-429,standing-cooldown]`, `test_ungated_host_429_still_halves_the_pacer` (the first two and standing-cooldown red at 951aae4). The review's sims now read: S2 collect 30/30 pages ok, `http_429` 1, pacer 0.952 rps; lookup 6/6 batches; OpenAlex 300 pages 0 failed in 150 s virtual. Open for Tomáš: the policy "a keyed provider's 429 = wait the cooldown, then resume at the base rate; only a 429 asking > 60 s halts" (this fix implements it for gate-paced families through `Transport`; S2 collect, whose pacing never halts, still fails a page on a cooldown > 60 s). | builder review-fix |
| D404 (review) | **A 200 carrying a provider error, or with an unreadable body, is a transient transport failure.** `stack/llm/__init__.py`: (1) L5-10: new `_provider_error_200(body)` = `bool(body.get("error")) or _finish_reason(body) == "error" or not isinstance(body.get("choices"), list) or not body["choices"]`; the call loop checks it first in the 200 branch, before the breaker reset and the schema checks, settles the attempt `http_5xx` at `_error_status_cost(body)` and goes through `_after_failure(state, "http_5xx", ...)`: retried with backoff, counted by the D400 breaker, `failed_transient[http_5xx]` (`AttemptsExhausted`) at worst, due again next run. Before, it was schema-retried twice, recorded `failed_permanent[schema_invalid]` (carried for ever by `prior_decision`), and each such 200 reset the breaker. A 200 with valid `choices` whose content fails the schema keeps the old behaviour. (2) L5-2 (S-28): `UrllibTransport._send` turns a 200 body that is not JSON, not UTF-8 or cut off (`ValueError`, `http.client.HTTPException` incl. `IncompleteRead`), or JSON but not an object, into `TransportError` ("unreadable 200 body"), retried as a network error, instead of an escaping exception that failed the run as `code_bug`. Why: findings L5-10, L5-2 (impl/25 review). Tests (`tests/test_llm_breaker.py`, red before the fix): `test_a_200_carrying_a_provider_error_is_transient_not_schema_invalid` (error object, finish error with/without error object, no choices), `test_an_incident_of_error_200s_at_32_workers_trips_the_breaker`, `test_an_unreadable_200_body_is_a_transport_error` (HTML, empty, not UTF-8, IncompleteRead); guard `test_a_genuine_schema_invalid_200_stays_permanent`. Also: `tests/test_screen_tiers.py` `test_tier2_invalid_or_oversize_response_keeps_borderline` now expects a tier-2 200 with an `error` body to be `failed_transient[http_5xx]` (was `failed_permanent[schema_invalid]`, the behaviour this row removes); and a D400 sibling missed in 940fc61: `test_transport_failures_fail_one_document_breaker_halts` (screen stage, client from `open_client`) was red under the 120 s minimum streak, so `LlmClient(min_failure_streak_s=None)` now reads `_MIN_FAILURE_STREAK_S` at construction and that test monkeypatches it to 0.0 to keep its count-only trip. Open: rows already written `schema_invalid` by such replies are found by `error LIKE '%response has no choices%' OR error LIKE '%not a JSON object%'` in `*_evidence` and need a reclassification or a pin change to be re-asked; batch-mode results are not covered by this check. | builder review-fix |
| D407 (review) | **A run's blob uploads go through a parallel uploader flushed before the publish (amends D360/D361's synchronous `put` for a run's store; finding L3-4, impl/25 review).** Measured in e2e build 1: `collect.openalex` ran 59 min for 663 pages, ~1.7 min of it paging; its 27,987 in-band blobs cost ~0.13 s each (a synchronous HEAD + PUT inside the page loop). `stack/store/blobs.py`: `BlobStore(store, *, deferred=False)` (and `open_blobs(root, *, deferred=False)`); deferred, on an S3 store, `put` hashes, writes the local copy at once (so `path`/`get` in the same run work, e.g. convert reading a blob acquire just stored) and queues the remote HEAD-then-PUT, deduped by digest within the process; `UPLOAD_THREADS = 16` daemon workers stream each blob from its local file (`put_file`, memory bounded); `flush()` waits for every queued upload and raises the first failure (again on every later call); `close(timeout)` drops queued uploads not started and joins the workers for at most `CLOSE_TIMEOUT = 30` s in all. A local-only store and every store opened outside a run (migrate, release, links, freeze, gate, build checks) stay synchronous. `stack/stage_runner.py`: `StageContext.blobs` is deferred; `run_stage` calls `job.check_cancel()` then `ctx._flush_blobs()` after staging and before `chain.publish` (before the claim, the rename of `data/.<name>.tmp`, the data PUTs and the record), also on the nothing-staged path before `end.ok()`; a failed upload ends the run `failed[code_bug]` with nothing renamed, as a failed synchronous PUT did (stricter in one case: a stage that caught a `put` error per item and went on now fails at the flush); `finally` closes the store on every outcome (a cancelled or failed run does not wait for its uploads). The publish order stays blobs, data, record; `run_recorded` (fold, migrate) has no deferred store. **D361 amended:** "a failed PUT leaves no local file" holds only for a synchronous store; in a run's store a local file can exist with no remote copy (a failed upload, a run killed before its flush), so a local file never proves an upload: every `put` (either mode) HEADs the remote, `missing()` (X5, `build_checks.py:371`) answers from one LIST and ignores local files, and the one `exists()` caller (`gate.load_gate`) only reads. Recovery and `stack store push` (job.py) are unchanged: a data file is renamed only after its run's flush, so no renamed, recovered or pushed data file names a blob its run did not upload; the no-upload path flushes too (blobs still go up, D361). Tests (`tests/test_store_job.py`, `SlowBlobS3`: 5 ms blob HEADs, blob PUTs held until the stage releases them): `test_a_runs_blob_puts_do_not_wait_on_the_remote` (red on the synchronous code: 12 puts took 6.13 s against a 0.25 s bound), `test_b_minted_blobs_go_up_before_the_data_and_the_record`, `test_c_a_failed_blob_upload_fails_the_run_and_publishes_nothing`, `test_d_a_run_dying_before_publish_leaves_local_blobs_a_later_put_uploads`, `test_blob_store_outside_a_run_is_synchronous`, `test_deferred_puts_from_threads_upload_each_digest_once`. Open for Tomáš: whether a pending-blob manifest (digests queued, not yet confirmed) should make recovery independent of a LIST; today nothing needs one, since only flushed runs rename data. | builder review-fix |
| D403 (review) | **An in-band body left `convert_pending` comes back into acquire's scope (scope clause `convert`; finding L4-8, impl/25 review).** A row triage does not let fetch whose current candidate a convert stop (`convert_max_rows`, `convert_max_minutes`, or under the defaults `max_rows`/the stage clock) left unconverted matched no scope clause from the next run on (minted, content current, nothing due, no text for `quality`), and convert walks only the scope: the body stayed `convert_pending` for good, never in corpus or screen, unreported; same for a `failed_transient` conversion. `workflows/acquire/scope.reasons` now appends `convert` when `pin is not None and c is not None and awaits_text(row, pin, structured)`, with `workflows/acquire/convert.awaits_text` = `any(not s.get("text_digest") and s.get("text_status") in (None, "failed_transient") for s in to_convert(row, pin, structured))`. Narrower than the review's `to_convert(...)` alone: a text converted under an older pin does not bring its row into scope. The clause goes through `select` like the others (counted `scope.convert`, `order`, filter, `max_rows`/`convert_max_rows` and the clocks apply unchanged); a row in scope for `convert` alone is never fetched (`permit` is not `fetch`, no role due). Side effect: a never-converted candidate convert cannot handle (`convert.no_tool`, `convert.blob_missing`) is now in scope and counted on every run instead of idle. Test `tests/test_acquire_convert.py::test_stopped_inband_conversions_come_back_into_scope` (three skip-decision in-band posts, run 1 `convert_max_rows=1`, run 2 converts the two left, trap lanes, `lane_calls` 0; a fourth post converted under `docling-v2` stays idle; red at 940fc61). Open for Tomáš: should a convert-pin change bring every old-pin text into scope (D9's intent), or stay opportunistic (re-converting only rows in scope for another clause, as now)? | builder review-fix |

When the cap fills inside the look-back (frontier not past the watermark), those hits are kept and the query is asked again from the watermark (counted `lookback_capped`), so the look-back cannot stall a query; holes are asked as before (no look-back). Applies when a build reads the watermark: no store rewrite; the next build of `main` recovers the e2e's own tail (submissions from 2026-10-10 on). Digests: none change: collectors have no `config_digest`, the coverage `query_digest` is the query text, and the default lives in code, so a plan's digest changes only if it sets the option. | D491 (fp-core) | **The series guard: `stack build` refuses, before any record, a build whose series has no `documents` file while another series of the store has one; `--new-series` allows it. A standalone `collect.*` run that pins no `sources` prior of its own and writes into such a series is refused the same way (`stack run --new-series`). (A1; S25-20; supersedes D378's "plan name = series" as the operating rule.)** Why: ids are minted per series (`Collector.source_id` reuses only the own chain's id in that series; `doc_id` = anchor member's `source_id`), so a build into a new series re-mints every id and re-pays every collect, triage, fetch and LLM call; nothing warned (std-v3 says `series: std-v3`, the e2e used `main`). `stack/stage_runner.py` `new_series_refusal(store, series)`: `None` without a series, when the series has a `documents` file, or when no series has one; else the message, naming the series that have `documents` and the flag. `stack/build.py` `run_build(new_series=)`: after `prepare`, before the record, raises `BuildFailed("new_series", …)` (the one refusal `run_build` raises; never recorded, so not in `BUILD_ERROR_CLASSES`); `run_passes` and `dry_run` take the flag (`dry_run`'s `new_series: {why, allowed}` or `None`, printed as the `new_series` line); the build's own runs get `new_series=True` (it asked the question of its series). `stack/cli/build.py` `--new-series`, the refusal as `error: build refused [new_series]: …`, exit 1; `stack/cli/run.py` `--new-series`. Refusal shape as the restart guard (`--restart`, `v4/OPERATE.md` standalone runs, "Restart"): before any work, the message naming the flag; no plan key (the flag is for one first build). Standalone runs: only collectors mint ids; gather, triage, acquire, annotate and the folds carry the ids they read, so they are not guarded. Criterion "no `documents` file" (the brief's): a series whose first build failed before gather has `sources` but no `documents`, and its rerun needs the flag again (harmless: its own chains keep the ids). Docs: `v4/OPERATE.md` (the build section's identity paragraph, `--new-series`, standalone "New series"), `v4/README.md` glossary, `configs/plans/README.md`, `v4/howto/full-run.md` step 3 (series `batch-import`, the full fetch's series, decided 2026-10-14). Tests: `tests/test_build_overrides.py` `test_build_into_a_new_series_beside_documents_is_refused_before_any_record`, `test_new_series_flag_starts_the_build`, `test_no_refusal_into_a_series_with_documents_or_in_an_empty_store`, `test_standalone_collector_run_into_a_new_series_is_refused`, `test_cli_new_series`; red with the guard disabled (3 failed, 2 passed). Not done: the plans' `series:` values (std-v3 still `std-v3`; the full-fetch plan names `batch-import`, A13, not this package). Default taken, for Tomáš: the flag name, collectors-only for standalone runs, the "no `documents` file" criterion. | builder fp-core |

A partial reversal of R8-1's blanket strip (D259); D591 is taken on another branch.** Why: with every credential stripped, fetchpdf's S2 lookups went to the shared keyless pool; build 4a's acquire runs counted `oa.rate_limited` 269 and 172, all from `api.semanticscholar.org` (live smoke 2026-10-17), and those 429s made the acquire tail slow. Unchanged: fetchpdf never sees a key (its `.env.local` is not loaded, its key constants stay `None`, its `HttpClient` strips credentials); the gate still strips every credential header and parameter from every request whoever added it, so OpenAlex, Crossref, Unpaywall, CORE, NCBI and publisher hosts get none, nor do other `*.semanticscholar.org` hosts. The key is put on the request only for its send, inside the Gate's slot (a Gate cooldown answer sends nothing and adds nothing), and removed from the request object afterwards, so the response fetchpdf receives (`resp.request`) and any redirect it follows carry none; the run cache key is the URL alone, the 429 records hold the URL, a transport error names only the URL. Tests (red before the change): `tests/test_provider_keys.py` `test_oa_gate_sends_our_s2_key_only_to_the_s2_api` (S2 keyed, the caller's own `x-api-key` replaced; OpenAlex with `Authorization` and `?api_key=`, Crossref, Unpaywall, CORE, `www.`/`pdfs.semanticscholar.org`, a publisher host with credentials: none sent; a cached repeat not counted; the 429's retries each keyed and counted; the key in neither `resp.request`, the cache, the 429 records, a transport error nor the counts), `test_oa_gate_without_an_s2_key_sends_none`, the slow fetchpdf probe amended (it asserted no `x-api-key` anywhere: now our key on the S2 API call only), `tests/test_acquire_lanes.py` `test_oa_lane_sends_our_s2_key_to_the_s2_api_only` (a run: S2 keyed, OpenAlex/Unpaywall not, `oa.http.s2_keyed` 1, the key in no file the run wrote). Mutations each fail a test: the host/family check removed (3), family without the host (1), the key left on the request (1), not counted (2), never attached (3), a constant key (the keyless test). Docs: the `stack/oa_adapter.py` and `stack/collect/provider_keys.py` docstrings, the lane's counts, `.env.example`, `v4/SETUP.md` §2. | D647 (export) | **Release format 2 and the internal export.** Release configs gain `audience` (`public|internal`, advisory; `internal` needs `--out` unless it ships no bytes: `content.select: none` and no `provider_records`), `filter` (a named filter or SQL over the **input** rows, applied before the rules; new named filter `screen_relevant` = screen `ok` and verdict `relevant`, borderline excluded), `snapshots: current|all` (default `current`: only the snapshot `content.current_snapshot_id` names, public-v1 included) and `content {select: none|text|all, place: blobs|inline, max_total_bytes (4 GiB), missing: fail|pointer, provider_records (false)}`; `excerpt_cap_chars` may be `null` (no cap). The **release schema only** (documents and corpus keep their names until a pipeline rename) names references by role and type: a blob reference is a struct `BLOB {sha256, bytes, media_type, inline}` (snapshot `digest`/`bytes`/`media_type` become `raw`, `text_digest` becomes `text` with `media_type` the raw's when the text is the raw bytes and those are `text/*`, else `text/markdown`, and `bytes` set when the export selected it; in-band entries' digests become `raw`/`text`), a flat string reference ends in `_sha256` (`content.current_text_sha256`, `current_text_media` kept; `identity.members[].inband_sha256s`), and `*_digest` means a fingerprint only; `inline` (nullable `large_binary`) holds the bytes under `place: inline`. Every family writer's S1 refuses `BLOB`/`inline`, so no build stage writes inline bytes; the footer lists the reference paths (`stack.blob_refs`) and `stack.blob_layout = blobs/<sha256>`; a release without `release_format: 2` (written before D647) is superseded: neither validated nor upcast (V10 lists it as a `warn`, `validate_release` reports only that; amended 2026-10-20, before merge: no release conversion, which is kept only for families the pipeline ingests from existing runs). Bytes ship per element when that element's own supplier has `text: ship` (a snapshot's `source_id`; the current text by `current_source_id`); in a shipped row a withholding member also loses its in-band entry digests and `inband_digests`. Shipped bytes go to `blobs/<sha256>` (the store grammar, no suffix) for every release, replacing `text/<digest>.md`; the data file stays `corpus.parquet` (1024-row groups, footer `stack.file_id = <run_id>.release`); `release.json` adds `release_format: 2, file_id, audience, filter, filter_checkable, source {file_id, path, family_version}, rows_in, filtered_out, classes` (kept rows per text-supplier class) and `content` (counts). `--out DIR` (`stack release`, `stack fold release`, and the alias `stack export`, default config `internal-v1`, no plan needed) writes a local directory, absent or empty: no run record, never pushed (both push paths bypassed), checked by `validate_release` before the rename. A pre-flight (local stat, else one LIST of the remote's `blobs/`) refuses a missing blob under `missing: fail` (`pointer`: listed in `missing-blobs.txt`) and a total over `max_total_bytes` (inline per element, `blobs/` per digest) before anything is written. `stack.checks.fold_checks.validate_release(dir)` serves V10, the writer and `stack verify --release DIR`; V10's `config_digest` is the sha256 of the JCS of the embedded config **as stored** (re-dumping through the current model would add defaulted keys and fail every older release). Readers: `stack.store.blobs.resolve(row, sha256, stores=[...])` (the BLOB's `inline`, then each named store root; `release.json` names no store, D540) and the duckdb macros `current_snapshot(d)`, `current_text(d)` (`stack/query.py`); the website query's shard key for the current text is `text_sha256` (renamed after the build: external consumers adapt to stack-v4 anyway). Dropping `inband` also drops `identity.members.inband_digests` (else 164k references would name digests the release lacks; a config file that drops `inband` must drop both; restored together with `inband` when `provider_records` is opted in); public-v1 changes accordingly. Both configs (and the model default) also drop `identity.members_digest` and `content.members_digest` (store change-detection hashes, nothing to a consumer). `provider_records: true` (needs `inband` kept) ships the `provider_record` in-band bodies to `blobs/`, inline into the entry's BLOB under `place: inline` (D522: not content; opt-in, recorded in `release.json`). New `configs/releases/internal-v1.yaml`: filter `screen_relevant`, every class but `shadow` `text: ship`, abstracts kept, no excerpt caps, `other: keep`, column drops only `inband`, `inband_digests` and the two `members_digest`s (keeps `run_id`s, `evidence_id`s, the screen reasoning, the `text_usability` note), the protective drops kept (masked, retired and sensitivity rows; `shadow` anchor rows dropped and `shadow`-supplied text withheld; 0 relevant rows affected when measured). public-v1 still ships no bytes (`text: pointer`): for it only the layout, the one-snapshot default and the `inband_digests` drop change (its config digest changes, as any config edit does). Deferred: a `columns` keep-list, a per-element predicate, a compression-level knob, in-band inline fields, an everything-config, reflink copies (no `text/` transition shim: older releases are superseded). Clarified 2026-10-20 by the pre-merge review fixes: SQL a config, plan, header or bundle supplies (a release or fold filter, a gate clause, a `links` rule) runs on a duckdb connection without file or network access, settings locked, as one statement (`stack.query.sql_connection`, `one_statement`), since `stack verify --release DIR` evaluates a bundle's `filter`; a release into the store is also validated over its stage before the rename (so before any push); `--out` must lie outside the store root; `column_drops` cannot drop the references the writer fills nor the fields the licence is read from (`KEPT_FIELDS`, and `KEPT_INBAND` while `inband` is kept; the `inband`/`inband_digests` pairing is the config model's, so an embedded config obeys it), nor `identity.is_masked` or `metadata.sensitivity` (`PRIVACY_FIELDS`: the validator's masked and sensitivity checks read them from the shipped rows and would pass vacuously without them; `state` may be dropped; test `tests/test_release_export.py::test_column_drops_keep_the_privacy_fields`, red before); `validate_release` classifies `release_format` first (above 2: newer than this code reads, a problem), reads only regular files that are not symlinks, and also checks a `blobs/`-placed BLOB's `bytes`, `schema_digest` (the file schema's), `filter` (the config's), `missing-blobs.txt` (sha256 lines of selected elements not in `blobs/`) and the `content` counters.
