| D650 (review-2) | **The SSRF guard blocks carrier-grade NAT, every address that is not globally reachable, IPv6 site-local, and an IPv6 address embedding an interior IPv4 one.** `stack/http.py` `_addr_is_interior` (used by `check_url_safety`: the urllib getter's redirect handler, the lanes before each call to the getter or a request of their own, the OA gate and the headless browser's request guard; the getter itself checks neither the initial URL nor the connected peer): besides the earlier `is_private`/loopback/link-local/reserved/multicast/unspecified, `not is_global`, explicit `100.64.0.0/10` (RFC 6598, Tailscale's addresses; neither private nor global on Python 3.12) and `fec0::/10` (`is_global` on 3.12), and the IPv4 address inside IPv4-mapped, 6to4 and NAT64 (`64:ff9b::/96`) addresses. NAT64 and 6to4 addresses are in fact refused as a class (on Python 3.12 every `64:ff9b::/96` address is `is_reserved` and every `2002::/16` one `is_private`, as before this row), so the embedded-IPv4 test decides IPv4-mapped addresses only; the lanes need an IPv4 route (on a DNS64/NAT64-only host every publisher's synthesised AAAA would be refused). A trailing dot on the host is stripped first (`localhost.`, `127.0.0.1.`, `foo.internal.` name the same hosts; review-2 B1). The IPv4 spellings `inet_aton` accepts (`127.1`, `0x7f000001`, `2130706433`, octal) are not `ipaddress` literals and are caught through the resolver (glibc parses them without DNS; pinned with the real resolver). Nothing blocked before is allowed now. Tests: `tests/test_fetch_http.py::test_check_url_safety` (CGNAT, the Tailscale resolver address, mapped CGNAT, site-local red before; mapped loopback, 6to4, NAT64, ULA and public controls) and `test_check_url_safety_resolves_rebinding` (a name resolving into 100.64/10); trailing-dot rows (red before the strip); `test_numeric_ipv4_spellings_are_blocked_through_the_real_resolver`. Unchanged: a resolution failure is allowed (proxied hosts), and the browser's redirect hops are watched, not refused (D590; the headless rung is off in every plan). | review fix, default taken, for Tomáš |
| D651 (review-2) | **The OA lane's request gate is its SSRF guard: on the `requests` path every request, each redirect hop and the connected address are checked and an interior one refused before it leaves; in fetchpdf's browser contexts routed requests are refused and redirect hops only detected; a refused URL is one failed candidate, and a role it decides ends `failed_permanent[blocked]`.** `stack/oa_adapter.py` `RequestGate.send` runs `stack.http.check_url_safety` (D650's classes; resolver `socket.getaddrinfo` on the network, none with an injected transport) on each `requests` call before the host's lock, after the run cache and the DataCite skip (no egress); `requests` sends a redirect hop through the adapter again, so each hop is its own check. A refused one raises `UnsafeURL` (a `requests` `InvalidURL`, not a `ConnectionError`: fetchpdf's client gives the URL up without its transient retries) and reaches no transport. On the network the gate also wraps `urllib3.util.connection.create_connection` (with `HTTPAdapter.send`, while a gate is active, routed per thread): a connection whose peer address is interior is closed before a byte is sent (DNS rebinding between the check's lookup and the connection's); the check is skipped only when the adapter connects through a proxy (`requests.utils.select_proxy` on the `proxies` it receives), as the urllib getter trusts the proxy; it does not compare the connection's host with the request's (urllib3 keeps a trailing dot, so `evil.example.` skipped the check before: review-2 B1); a peer address that cannot be read (the server already closed the socket) is closed and surfaces as a transient `ConnectionError`, not a refusal (review-2 S2). Playwright's `Browser.new_context`/`new_page` and `BrowserType.launch_persistent_context` are wrapped likewise: a context fetchpdf opens under the gate gets the headless rung's guard (`stack.browser.guard_context`, factored out of `_render`; `service_workers="block"`, overriding the caller's choice). `guard_context` also refuses service-worker registration in every document (an init script locking `ServiceWorkerContainer.prototype.register`): on Playwright 1.62 `block` only replaces `navigator.serviceWorker.register` on the instance and stops Playwright attaching to workers, so a worker registered through the prototype's method fetched past routing (checked with real Chromium: its fetch to an interior host reached the server; under `allow` the same fetch was routed and aborted). Playwright's `APIRequestContext` (`page.request`, `context.request`) is not routed; under the gate its methods check the request's URL (`RequestGate.check_api_request`, recorded `browser_api`), not the redirects Playwright follows for it. fetchpdf's SSRN branch launches Chromium whether or not `oa_playwright` is set, so this is live in the default plan. Refusals are recorded per thread (`RequestGate.blocked`, `take_blocked`; counts `oa.http.blocked`, `oa.http.blocked_browser`). Lane (`workflows/acquire/lanes/oa.py`): a refused URL in a step is inconclusive (the next OA location, step or the walk is tried), and is not stored as a run negative; a walk in which a browser redirect hop reached an interior host has its artifacts discarded (`oa.walk_discarded`: Playwright cannot refuse a hop, D590); a role with no artifact ends `failed_permanent[blocked]` naming the URL (`url_unsafe:blocked`) when a request, connection, browser main-frame navigation (`browser_nav`, review-2 N7), Playwright API request or browser hop of its steps was refused, after `rate_limit` and the transient classes the steps recorded, before `no_fetchable_url`. The transient precedence holds for Zenodo, MDPI, the direct PDF candidates and the walk; Unpaywall folds a per-location 403/5xx/timeout into `inconclusive` (pre-existing: before this row such a role ended `no_fetchable_url`, also 90 days), so beside an interior Unpaywall location it does not outrank the refusal (review-2 S3; the narrowing is the default taken, the fix queued in `v4/FUTURE.md` since it also moves non-SSRF outcomes). A redirect to a non-http scheme (`InvalidSchema`/`MissingSchema` inside `requests`, no egress) is an inconclusive step, not a `network` transient (review-2 N1). Existing class (`blocked`, as the http and arXiv lanes give an unsafe URL), so no schema or vocabulary change; rechecked after 90 days like any `blocked` role. A browser subresource the guard aborted only counts. Why: the URLs come from provider records (Unpaywall OA locations, Zenodo files, landing pages) and the OA lane had no SSRF check. Tests: `tests/test_fetch_oa.py` (the D651 block: literal private, metadata, CGNAT, IPv4-mapped, NAT64, 6to4, ULA, interior names; public controls incl. 100.128.0.1; a redirect hop to a private and to a CGNAT-resolving host; names resolving private, CGNAT and mapped loopback; a name the guard sees public that connects to a loopback server; an interior Unpaywall location, an interior URL beside a public copy and beside a 403, an interior URL inside the walk, a walk with a leaked browser hop) and `tests/test_browser.py::test_the_oa_gate_guards_the_browser_contexts_opened_under_it` (real Chromium, local server); red before (the interior URLs reached the transport), and each of the URL check, connect check, browser wrap, discard and outcome turns its tests red when removed. Limits: a request fetchpdf made on a thread of its own would pass unguarded and unpaced (it starts none in retrieval today); a resolution failure is allowed by the URL check (the connect check then sees the real address). The browser side is best-effort: a browser redirect hop is still sent (detected, the walk discarded), Chromium does its own name lookups (a host the guard saw public can be rebound interior unseen), hop verdicts are cached per host, and an `APIRequestContext` redirect is unchecked (fetchpdf uses it only on the batch CLI's supplementary Dataverse path, unreachable from `retrieve_tiered`). The default plan's browser entry points are fetchpdf-built URLs on known hosts (SSRN abstract pages, Wiley full-text pages; OSF and publisher pages only with `oa_playwright`, off in every plan), so the residual risk needs a page or an open redirect on those publishers; provider-record URLs go through `requests`, where hops are refused and peers checked. Before any plan enables broader browser navigation (`oa_playwright`, the http lane's `headless`), the Chromium process needs isolation (a network namespace or firewall denying interior ranges), queued in `v4/FUTURE.md`. Review-2 tests: `tests/test_fetch_oa.py::test_the_connected_address_is_checked_too` (`rebind.test.`, `REBIND.test`; the dotted case red before), `::test_a_connection_to_a_configured_proxy_is_not_peer_checked`, `::test_an_unreadable_peer_is_a_transient_connection_error_not_a_refusal`, `::test_a_redirect_to_a_non_http_scheme_is_inconclusive_not_a_network_transient`, `::test_an_aborted_main_navigation_decides_the_role_a_subresource_does_not`; `tests/test_browser.py::test_the_oa_gate_checks_playwright_api_requests`, `::test_a_guarded_context_refuses_service_worker_registration` (real Chromium, red under `block` alone), `::test_the_oa_gate_guards_a_persistent_context_and_records_an_aborted_navigation`, `::test_the_oa_gate_forces_service_workers_block_on_every_door`; each red before its fix (or under a mutation removing it). | review fix, default taken, for Tomáš; review-2 follow-ups (S3 narrowed, not fixed; the service-worker lockdown) defaults taken, for Tomáš |
| D652 (verify-speed) | **Verify reads projected fields, decides columnar where it can, and runs a build's check by default, a structural check at each build's start and finish, and a full verify only when asked; nothing carries over from one verify to the next (decided by Tomáš 2026-10-21; supersedes D281's incremental pair checks).** Why: builds 2a and 2b of the 2015 backfill (159,059 documents, every `batch-import` file a full file) spent about 2.5 h each in verify, and 2b's held 13.9 GB RSS plus 3.75 GB swap. Measured on a local copy of the store, the old code's time went to the file-scope loop (S1-S10, V1-V6, V9 over every data file of the build's families on every verify: ~65 min), V7/V8 over every `<wf>`/evidence file (~3 min each), the pair checks converting whole blocks of every compared row to Python (X17 292 s, X24 116 s, X19 105 s, X13 68 s for 4 new files) and X4 (155 s); the memory to X6-X8 holding every run's whole corpus as Python rows (X8 alone passed 14 GB RSS plus swap before it was stopped). (1) **Primitive**: `stack.store.parquet.field_paths` / `project_schema` / `project` / `read_family_fields`: dotted paths into `struct` and `list<struct>` columns (`identity.members_digest`, `identity.members.source_id`), a file read one top-level column at a time and narrowed, so memory follows the projected fields; `read_view(columns=)`, `StoreView.read/table/view_at` take such paths; `StoreView.base_join(df, fields)` joins a chain file with its base view on `doc_id` (aligned tables, file row order), and `base_pairs` is built on it. (2) X19, X4, X13, X24 and X5 read only the fields they compare; X19 compares the digests columnar and asks `is_forward` once per distinct move; X4 counts live members columnar; X17 compares a block (as Python values, as before) only on rows whose block stamps differ, the only rows where "unchanged but restamped" can hold; X15 and X9 hold one block / one fold at a time; X9 skips a batch whose two sides are equal Arrow tables. (3) X6-X8: the corpus input read narrowed to `CORPUS_FIELDS` (the fields `select` and the basis functions read, pinned by a key-access test; plus the whole `annotations` block for a run with joined reads or a `chained` basis), once per check; the runs yielded one at a time; the records of one producer run share its evidence rows; X6 reads no corpus. (4) **Parts and full.** A verify runs some of three parts, or everything. **structural**: file damage over the whole store, from footers, records, headers, the chains' key columns and the S3 listing, never a data file in full: S1 from each file's footer, V11 (chains resolve; keys unique and `ids_digest` recomputing in the files from the newest full file to the head), X23, X1 (every recorded file present, its footer's row count the record's, on a mirror its size the S3 object's; no re-hash) and X5 (every referenced blob listed, a raw snapshot's `bytes` its blob's size). **files**: every check on the files a build's runs wrote (the file checks, the pair checks against their base views, V7/V8), or those of `--run` runs. **build_set**: the other build checks (X2-X25 less the structural ones) on that build. **`stack verify`** (the default) runs files and build_set on the newest finished build, `ok` or `incomplete` (never `failed`, `cancelled` or `running`), which is also the build checks' reference (X2, X10's `version_chain`, X14; X23 judges each file and needs none), or on `--build` (an id, a record path or `latest`, the newest `ok` build as `stack release` reads it), or on the newest finished build of `--series S`; `--no-build-set` leaves the build set out; `--structural` runs only the structural part. **A build** runs the structural part after its preflight and before any run (a hard failure ends it `failed[verify]` with no run; the record's `verify_start`), and all three parts at its finish (`verify`). **Full** (`stack verify --full`, `stack build --verify-full`): every check on every file and every local data file re-hashed; explicit only, too slow for a default, to be run later by a schedule that never overlaps a build. A check of a part not run is `skipped[<part>]`; `verify` and `verify_start` are `{status, mode, checks}`, the mode `full` or the parts joined by `+`. The structural checks find damage to files and blobs, not what a build or a code change got wrong; the build's check finds that in what the build wrote. Removed: the code digest over the file checks' modules (`file_checks_code`, 83 of 144 modules: almost any commit re-ran every file check, and the dependency was invisible from the code that triggered it), the per-check verified-file lists in build records (736 KB per record on the 2b replay, derived state, invalidated by any re-keying), `PAIR_CHECKS_VERSION`, `verify.pairs` and the reference-build lookup of D281. The reason is that code changes often and data files and blobs can be corrupted independently of it, so no verify trusts an earlier one's verdicts. **Limits**: after a change to a check, the registry or a schema, old files are re-judged only by the next full verify; a same-size corruption of a data file, and a text blob's or an in-band entry's size (none is recorded; the planned blob rename adds a size field), are caught by no structural check; a file written outside a build (`stack run`, a migrate) is checked by `stack verify --run` or the next full verify; damage arising between builds is seen at the next build's start. (5) `read_view` of one full file without a key filter reads it once (no row selection, no two copies) when its keys ascend; `fold.filter_rows` keeping every row does not copy; `StoreView.drop_cache` releases Arrow's freed memory; a data file whose footer does not read is left out of the view and is X1's finding (it used to crash verify). (6) **Measured** on the 2b replay (a local copy; X1 and X5 fail on the copy only, for every mode and for old and new code alike: a release file and 254,340 blobs live on S3 and the copy has no remote): the structural part **18.6 s, peak 1.5 GB** (X5 15 s, the rest under 2 s); the three parts on build 2b (16 files, what 2b's finish runs) **859 s, 3.5 GB** (the file loop over its files 322 s, the build checks and the pair checks on its files the rest; X14 60 s, X4 53 s, X12 51 s, X8 47 s, X21 43 s), so the default `stack verify` of 2b is about 840 s (inferred: the same run less the structural checks); full **6,702 s (1 h 52 min), 3.6 GB** (the file loop over 499 files 3,935 s; the pair checks over every chain file X15 724 s, X17 441 s, X13 303 s, X24 284 s, X19 139 s; V7/V8 185/205 s; hashing every data file 19 s with the files in the page cache; run beside another full test suite for about 25 of its minutes). Old code: 2a 2.6 h and 2b 2.5 h in the backfill, 2b's verify 13.9 GB RSS plus 3.75 GB swap; on the replay, X8 alone passed 14 GB RSS plus swap and was stopped. Per check, old to new (4 new documents files): X19 105 to 9 s, X17 292 to 26 s, X24 116 to 18 s, X13 68 to 15 s, X4 155 to 52 s, X9 195 to 34 s, X5 58 to 15-19 s. The X5 LIST of `blobs/` on S3 is not in these numbers (the copy is local); one LIST of the production store's 462,886 blobs took 69 s (measured by another agent the same day), so the structural part there is about 1.5 min. (7) **Equivalence**: the replaced row-wise code kept as references in `tests/test_verify_projected.py` (equal findings item for item on the clean store, each check's fixture and planted faults; key-access tests pin the projections). On the replay: old and new code, every file check run, 44 checks (all but X6-X8, which the old code cannot finish there): 0 differ; X6-X8 of the new code against the same code reading the whole corpus per run: equal. Planted on a copy: one `acquired -> triaged` in 2b's last acquire file (X19 flags it, old and new, the same item) and one edited `screen` verdict (X8 flags it, new and whole-corpus reference, the same item). | Tomáš 2026-10-21 (builder verify-speed, verify-modes) |

| D666 (manual-fields) | **A manual source can carry its own `title`, `authors` and `published_at`: optional fields of a `manual_sources` entry, written by `collect.manual` into its `sources` row's `metadata` (the slots every collector fills) and merged by gather like any member's metadata; the prepared files `configs/overrides/manual_sources.yaml` and `configs/overrides/lineage_origins.yaml` carry them for every `accept` entry.** Amends D658's and D664's limit "no title, authors or date until a `fields` override" (complexity review F13). **Mechanics.** `stack.overrides.ManualSource` takes the three fields (`MANUAL_FIELDS`), kept in the row's payload only when given, so an entry without them keeps its payload and the overrides digest. One validator, `stack.overrides.field_value`, now reads both a `fields` override's value (gather's `_coerce`, moved there unchanged in behaviour) and a manual source's fields, so the add refuses what gather would refuse: a timestamp is an ISO date or time (a YAML year number, which pydantic would read as a Unix time, and a bare `"2015"` are refused; a year alone is written `<year>-01-01`, which gather's merge already reads as year-only), authors are names or `{name, orcid, affiliation_raw}`, a title is non-empty text; a revoke carries no fields; the CSV form carries them in `payload`. `collect.manual` adds the typed fields to the row's `metadata` (`origin: human`) and the given fields to its record (so a changed field writes a new row, an unchanged entry none). Before, the manual channels were unranked like blogs and cards and a tie went to the newer row, so the title could flip with each re-observation. The rank digest, part of gather's `config_digest`, changes with it. The paper matchers now see a `manual_paper` source's title and authors like any paper's. **Not added:** a DOI or arXiv id field. The schema's slot for them is an identity key, but on a `manual_url` source (an author-hosted PDF) a `doi` key merges nothing (the url group merges on `url` keys only) while `collect.openalex-lookup` would look it up and mint a separate paper document: a duplicate. A work that should be keyed by its DOI or arXiv id takes that URL as the entry's `url` (as before). **Migration.** 85 entries got title and date, 79 also authors: the 60 `accept` entries of `manual_sources.yaml` (titles and dates from the notes, corrected by the PDFs' first pages where they differ: 4 titles reworded (among them `TechnicalAgenda.pdf`, which now serves the 2017 retitled version, dated by its 2014 release), 4 completed from a truncated note (one from the old FHI URL's slug), diacritics restored, 1 author (the Distributions Allowing Tiling note is Yudkowsky's, not Fallenstein's); dates as the earliest public day the PDF, the note or the MIRI announcement post that released the PDF gives, else the note's year as `<year>-01-01`; authors only where a PDF, an arXiv page or the note names them in full) and the 25 of `lineage_origins.yaml` (note titles and years; author names from the OpenAlex records fetched for D664, the PDFs or the note). A store that already holds an entry picks its fields up through a new entry `supersedes:` it with the fields: the next `collect.manual` writes a new row for that source, gather changes the document's metadata and `fields_digest`, and triage re-decides the row; for an `accept` row the rule decides (no LLM call), any other row is asked again (about $0.16 per 1,000 rows); screen does not re-run (its basis is the text). **Tests:** `tests/test_collect_manual.py`: the fields validated, kept in the payload only when given, refused for 9 bad forms (also by gather for a `fields` override); the scenario collects an entry with the fields into `sources` metadata, record and the document's metadata (`field_sources` origin `human`), and a superseding entry adds a title to a collected paper (4 rows written, 1 unchanged); `…::test_gather_ranks_a_manual_title_after_every_collected_one` (a blog's and a card's title win over a newer manual row; alone, the manual title stands and beats a link anchor; red before the rank change, and with the manual channels placed after the link channels); the prepared file: every `accept` entry has a title and a date, no post has fields, 6 entries pinned as read off their PDFs. `tests/test_overrides.py`: the CSV twin carries the fields. `tests/test_overrides_lineage_origins.py`: every manual source has title and authors, its date the note's year. A reference is named by its role (`raw`, `text`), a flat string reference ends in `_sha256`, `*_digest` is a fingerprint. `INBAND_ENTRY = (source_id!, content_role!, raw BLOB, text BLOB, captured_at!)` (was `raw_digest, text_digest, media_type!`): `text.media_type` is the entry's for a text-only entry, `text/markdown` when both are set (the X collector, whose mint names `text_media_type`). `SNAPSHOT.digest/bytes/media_type` → `raw!: BLOB`, `text_digest` → `text: BLOB` (`stack.schemas.structs.text_blob`: the raw's media type when the text is the raw bytes and those are `text/*`, else `text/markdown`), `convert_config_digest` → `convert_pin`; `CONTENT.config_digest` → `convert_pin`, `current_text_digest` → `current_text_sha256`; `MEMBER.inband_digests` dropped (write-only, derivable). `BLOB.bytes` is non-null: collectors record the length at mint, `convert` the converter output's, lanes the fetched size; acquire's `inband` substage takes the entry's BLOBs and no longer reads a blob to size it (`inband_blob_missing` gone: X5 reports a missing blob). `QUALITY.tier` (the stamp's `+tier<k>`, `stack.conversion.ladder.stamp_tier`, written by `apply_verdict`): D661's garbled retry reads `tier != RAW_TIER` instead of the stamp's suffix. `ROLE.rule` (`arxiv_pdf` when the arXiv PDF rule set the status; NULL after any lane outcome, `fetchcycle._attempted`): the rule recognises its own skips by it, no longer by the `arxiv_pdf:` error prefix (the text stays, for humans). `current_text_media` keeps its rule (`txt` for an in-band `text/plain` body; a fetched plain-text page that converts to itself is `md` although its `text` BLOB is `text/plain`). Gate view column `inband_text_digest` → `inband_text_sha256` (9 plan SQL lines; every plan's gate digest moves, so triage re-decides each triaged row once with no LLM call, plan 69 §9.1); a gate stored before the rename (the blobs `store_gate` wrote, read only by X14) names the old column, and `load_gate` reads it under the new name (the blob and its digest stay; rewriting them would change every build record's `gate_digest` for no gain); this read is not part of the one-off upcast and stays as long as X14 must read the gate of any pre-rename build; `inband_excerpt_digest` → `inband_excerpt_sha256`; `topic_digest` → `topic_record_sha256`. S6 checks `sha256`, `*_sha256` and `convert_pin` as 64-hex. **Checks:** X5 walks every BLOB of a row (`stack.schemas.structs.blob_refs`, the one locator of a row's references) and compares its `bytes` with the store's listing, plus `current_text_sha256` and the pin; V6 adds `current_text_media` = the pointer's `media_of` and one size per blob (a text that is its raw records the raw's bytes); V1, V4, V9, X24, X25 and the release validator read the new names. **Release** (format 2; `releases/` on the store was empty on 2026-10-21, so the column renames break no published release): the release `BLOB` is the pipeline's plus `inline`, every field nullable (a withheld snapshot keeps `raw` with `sha256` NULL and loses `text`, a withheld in-band entry loses both); the D647 translation layer (renames in `release_row`, `FLAT_REFS`, `_BLOB_FIELDS`, `_FOLDED`, `_RELEASE_KEYS`, the either-form `ref_sha256`/`current_text_ref`, `INBAND_DIGESTS` and its `column_drops` pairing) is gone, so `selected_refs` and `release_row` read one form in either order (complexity review F7); `text.bytes` is the corpus's; `column_drops` cannot drop a kept reference's `sha256` (path, ancestor, `*.sha256`). The release schemas of internal-v1 and public-v1 differ from cee8d92's only in `content.convert_pin`, `snapshots[].convert_pin`, `snapshots[].quality.tier`, `roles[].rule`. `stack show` prints the recorded sizes (no blob lookup); its `--json` report changes shape (in-band entries and snapshots as BLOBs, `provider_records[].sha256`, `current.text_sha256`; no in-repo consumer). Not renamed: fingerprints, eval item keys (`input.text_digest`), payload JSON (the affiliation grounding), the lanes' own snapshot dict (converted at `acquire._snapshot`), history. **Tests:** `tests/test_blobrefs_upcast.py`, `tests/test_upcast_blob_refs_tool.py`, `tests/test_blob_ref_names.py` (no old name in `stack/`, `workflows/`, `tools/` outside the one-off upcast and an allow-list; red before the checks port), `tests/test_verify_modes.py::test_x5_checks_every_blobs_size` (red with raw-only sizes), the suite ported. **Measured** (copy of the mirror, newest documents file, 159,059 rows): old code on the v5 file and new code on its v6 upcast decide the same per row (acquire scope, convert selection, pointer fields, annotate bases, gate excerpt): the outputs are byte-identical. | Tomáš 2026-10-20 (plan 69 defaults; (i) rename the gate column) and 2026-10-21 (sizes required; the two markers as fields; F7 inside the rename) |
| D691 (blob-refs) | **Older documents/corpus/sources files are rewritten once on disk, not upcast on read.** v6/v4 sit behind `Incompatible(BLOB_REFS_REASON)`: every reader refuses an older file and names `tools/upcast_blob_refs.py`. The tool runs `sizes` (one LIST of `blobs/`, read-only client), `plan` (dry run in memory, read-only), `archive --name` (mirror only: server-side copies of every target data file and every record to `archive/<name>/<store prefix>/`, a LIST check of size and single-part ETag; an archive name that holds objects is refused) and `apply` (refused while a job is live; on a mirror unless the archive holds every target and record as the manifest says and the store still holds each object not yet rewritten as archived; and when the dry run refuses a file or misses a size), then `stack verify --full`. `plan` (and `apply`'s dry run) checks every row of every file old against new (`blobrefs_upcast.check`: per-row list lengths, every sha256, every size against the listing, media types, `tier` and `rule` recomputed from the old columns; a snapshot raw the listing lacks is refused although it records its bytes, being a lost blob), since verify reads only the build's head and corpus and no check reads media types, tiers or rules. `--work` is required and bound to the store (`before.json` names it); a record entry is patched from the digest `before.json` took or the record's own at the run's start; a second live-job check runs before the records are patched, and at the end every record entry naming a target must name its new digest. `apply` rewrites each target in place (same key, file id and header but `schema_digest`/`family_version`; through `write_family`, so S1-S10 run on it), stages, pushes and then replaces files and records, and patches the run records' `outputs` and `in_files` and the build records' `files` entries that name a rewritten file at its old digest; a journal (`before.json`, `journal.jsonl`) makes a re-run continue. Other mirrors follow by themselves (a record whose LIST entry changed is re-fetched; an old data file is moved aside on its digest mismatch). `stack/schemas/blobrefs_upcast.py` holds the old types (they render to the registered v5/v3 digests), the arrow-native step (only visible list items are read) and its guards (an in-band entry with neither digest; a member list that is not its entries'; a blob without a size; a required field NULL in a valid row); `upcasters.upcast(..., end=)` runs the older steps to v5/v3. Delete the module, the tool and the older version entries once every store is upcast. **Dry run** on a local copy of the mirror (242 files: documents v3 78 / v5 32, corpus v3 30 / v5 15, sources v3 87): sizes from one LIST of 462,886 blobs (69 s); 242 upcast, 0 refused, 419,228 sizes filled, 0 missing; 12,949,140 rows; 430 records (1,301 entries) patched; 29 min, peak RSS 5.2 GB; every one of 65,246,387 references in the upcast files has the listed size. `stack verify --full` on the upcast copy (106 min on a shared box): 45 of 47 ok; X5 red only on blobs the copy does not hold locally (all on the store's listing at their recorded size); X14 red from code before the stored-gate read, ok with it. | Tomáš 2026-10-20 ((m): a one-off on-disk upcast, archive first, verify after, in a no-build window) |

(2) Transport: `llm.yaml` 3.6.0 adds `providers.openai` (base URL of the OpenAI API, key `OPENAI_API_KEY` by name, `dialect: openai`, `strip_model_prefix: openai/`) and roles `extract_staged_openai` / `extract_main_openai` (gpt-6-luna, `provider: openai`, no fallbacks); plan batch-2026-10a revision 7's technique_staged / model_roles pins name them. A role's `provider` is a transport choice in no digest or cache key: the two stages' config digests move only by the role name in the pin; screen, affiliation (still extract_main) and triage keep theirs (computed before / after: screen 63dc7d28…, affiliation 744785dd…, triage 8a4c4ba0…). (3) Cost: a reply without `usage.cost` (OpenAI's) is priced from `pricing`, with gpt-6-luna's cached-input $0.01, cache-write $0.125 and above 272k prompt tokens $0.20 / $0.75 / $0.02 / $0.25 per 1M (OpenAI pricing page, standard tier, 2026-10-24); OpenRouter's `usage.cost` on the gold-v3 eval calls equals these list prices to the cent (a fitted 0.1x read / 1.25x write; one call recomputed exactly). (4) Schemas: OpenAI refuses technique_staged's single / glean schemas in strict mode (HTTP 400, "'additionalProperties' is required to be supplied and to be false" at the root; every eval call paid this 400, then degraded); on the `openai` dialect a schema that is not strict-shaped (`is_strict_schema`) is sent folded into the prompt from the first attempt, the degrade's request byte for byte, so no digest moves and no call pays the round trip; model_roles' schema is strict and keeps `response_format`. | D717 (annotations-1.0) | **An override that supplies the whole payload of a `<wf>` row is the decision: the row and the folded `annotations.<wf>` take its provenance, not the selected evidence's.** Why: the 21 stand-in answers (`ai_check` row overrides of model_roles and technique_staged for the 17 documents luna refused with HTTP 400, author `ai:claude-<model>`, a note with model and method) would otherwise fold with luna's `config_digest`, `decided_at` and failed `evidence_id`, as if luna had answered. A field override over the model's payload keeps the evidence's provenance. V7 (`stack/checks/annotate.py`) accepts an `ok`/`empty` non-human row without evidence when it lists `override_ids`. X8 reproduces the rows (deterministic). No schema change: the ANN common fields have no author/note field, so `author` and `note` stay on the override row, reached through the `<wf>` file's `override_ids`; they do not reach the corpus or a release. Consequences: a reader pinning by config digest (`ann_pinned`, `stack.annotations.annotation(..., config_digest=)`) no longer matches an override-supplied record (no pipeline stage does); an annotation record (`model_regexp_matches`) takes only its own overrides, so a model_roles row override leaves it `failed_permanent` with a NULL payload and the producer's evidence provenance. Also: D714 (1) said a luna failure is failed_transient; a 4xx luna keeps refusing (the 17 HTTP 400s) is failed_permanent[query_invalid] and not re-asked (D714 stands as decided; this row corrects it, and the batch-2026-10a comment is corrected). Tests: `tests/test_annotate.py` `test_override_supplied_row_carries_the_overrides_provenance`, `test_override_supplied_items_carry_the_overrides_provenance`, `test_override_row_wins` (now expects the override's provenance); `tests/test_checks_annotate.py` `test_v7_an_ok_ai_row_without_evidence_needs_override_ids`; red without the change. | Tomáš (2026-10-25) |

| D722 (providers) | **Several LLM providers per prompt: a provider-qualified model reference, the Anthropic Messages API as a third dialect, egress by a direct provider's slug (amends D714's routing; Tomáš: "AI providers: Ideally we can use at least OpenRouter and OpenAI API directly, possibly with Anthropic API. Can be set in the prompt model config (so model name may be provider-dependent).").** (1) Routing (`LlmConfig.route`): a model reference `<provider>:<model id>` (an `llm.providers` key, no `/` before the `:`; OpenRouter's `vendor/model:free` is not one) goes to that provider wherever a model is named (a role's `model` / `fallbacks`, a pin's `model` / `adjudicate_model` / `prepass_model` / `select_model`), so a pin switches a stage's provider without a new role or a workflow change; an unqualified id goes to the role's `provider` (D714), else the default (OpenRouter). The reference as written is the model in every digest and the response-cache key (as an unqualified id always was; a role's `provider` stays in none), so `anthropic:claude-opus-5-5` and a role `{provider: anthropic, model: claude-opus-5-5}` are two configs with two digests: spell a stage's model one way. Model ids are the provider's own (`claude-sonnet-4-6` on the Anthropic API, `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6` on OpenRouter). Prices: the reference's entry, else its bare id's. A reference the client cannot route (unknown qualifier), or a role setting its route's dialect refuses, fails at `llm.yaml` load or, for a pin's reference, as `RouteInvalid` (fatal, config_missing) before the cache and any request. Batch mode refuses any direct route (as D714). (2) Egress: a direct provider's `egress_provider` is the slug the gate checks for every model it serves (`openai`, `anthropic`); OpenRouter keeps the model-prefix map and its `provider.only` pin. The Anthropic API is gated like `anthropic/...` on OpenRouter: open, public_web, restricted and api_tos, not shadow. (3) The `anthropic` dialect (plain HTTP like the other two: no SDK dependency, `uv.lock` unchanged): `POST /v1/messages`, the key in `x-api-key`, `anthropic-version: 2026-10-21` (which refuses any `temperature`: refused at load for this dialect, as is effort `minimal`); the fixed prefix as the `system` text block with a `cache_control` breakpoint; the per-call turns as text blocks, consecutive same-role turns merged (the schema-retry and fold turns follow a user turn); `output_config.format` = the wire schema without `minimum` / `maximum` (the API takes no numerical constraints; the client still validates them) and `output_config.effort` when the role sets one (no `thinking` field: adaptive thinking is the current models' default); a top-level `cache_control` (cached through the last block, so a gleaning turn reads the document) unless `cache_prefix_only` (model_roles: only the prefix is written); a non-strict schema goes folded from the first attempt (the API requires closed objects, as OpenAI's strict mode, D714); `stream: true` on the provider: server-sent events reassembled by the transport (`assemble_sse`), since a non-streamed call idles until done and long ones drop at about 10 minutes. (4) Replies: read through `anthropic_view` (text blocks joined, thinking dropped; `stop_reason` end_turn / stop_sequence = stop, max_tokens = truncated, the doubled-cap retry as before; `prompt_tokens` = `input_tokens` + `cache_read_input_tokens` + `cache_creation_input_tokens`, the latter two as `tokens_cached` / `tokens_cache_write`; no reasoning-token count); the response digest and cache entry keep the raw body; cost from `pricing` with the cache rates. `stop_reason: refusal`: a paid attempt (`error_class` refused), then the next model if the call has one, else `ProviderRefused` = failed_permanent[query_invalid], never schema-retried. Statuses: 429 and 529 / 5xx and a stream's error event retried as rate_limit / http_5xx; 401 / 402 / 403 fatal; 413 and a 400 "prompt is too long" too_large. (5) `llm.yaml` 3.7.0: `providers.anthropic` (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, streamed), `egress_provider: openai` on `providers.openai`, prices of `claude-opus-5-5` ($4 / $20, cache read $0.20, 5-minute write $5), `claude-sonnet-5-5` ($2 / $10, $0.20, $2.50) and `claude-haiku-5-5` ($0.10 / $0.50, $0.01, $0.125; above 100K prompt tokens $0.50 / $2.50 / $0.05 / $0.625), from the claude-api reference shipped with Claude Code (2026-10-26), not yet checked against the live pricing page. No role names Anthropic and no plan pins it: choosing a model and a stage is open. (6) Unchanged, checked before / after (5afa9d1 → this change): the wire request and template / model / rendered digests of every 3.6.0 role through a fake call, the gated models per license class, and every plan's annotation config digests (batch-2026-10a: technique_staged `afc8e6f6…`, model_roles `bb1fcb36…`, screen `63dc7d28…`, affiliation `744785dd…`); the role and pin values are golden in `tests/test_llm_anthropic_direct.py`. Not changed: the default provider's key is still required by `open_client` (OPENROUTER_API_KEY) even for a stage whose calls are all direct; finish_reason `content_filter` on the chat-completions dialects is not mapped to a refusal; the ledger label stays `openrouter/<model>`. | conductor (providers) |

| D724 (triage-all) | **Triage asks every document its questions, also outside the question scope (a `sql:`/`rule:` fetch, or a primary role that is `ok`, i.e. a document that already has text); an answer there is stored as a *signal* and decides nothing, so every decision and everything downstream (acquire's `permit`, fetch, convert, `fold.corpus`, the screen) is as before. Amends D697 (a carried open answer outside the question scope is asked again when an asker runs; settled with the fill only when none does), the asker protocol (it gets every scoped row lacking a final answer, in the stage's order) and D161 (C)'s triage scope (adds answers due).** Why (Tomáš, 2026-10-26): triage was only a fetch filter; on the head of build ws1qpn8myzxah only 149,644 of 215,091 live documents had a verdict under the current question digest, 8,546 of the 73,655 corpus documents; a verdict on every document gives triage's precision/recall against the screen on fetched documents and allows later policies; a re-triage of everything must be a normal operation. **Signal** (`stack.gate.signal_row`): the question row keeps the fill `select` gives it there (`skipped[not_needed]`, `skipped[not_requested]` without the ask substage) and records the answer's `verdict`, `confidence` and `evidence_id` (a non-`ok` answer: its `evidence_id` only); `decide()` and X14's recompute read `status`/`error_class` only, so a signal decides as the plain fill did, by construction, and X14/X13/V5 are unchanged; `gate.verdict_of` reads a document's verdict whatever the status; a signal is carried as the `ok` answer it records (`carried_answers`), so a row that enters the question scope later decides on it without a call. A carried real answer outside the question scope (asked while the row was in it) is kept and decides as before. **Due** (`stack.gate.answer_due`, count `answers_due`; when an asker will run): a live row on its current triage basis lacking a settled answer: no row of the current question digest, or a fill that is not a settled signal (a verdict; evidence the retry rule carries, a due transient or evidence missing from the prior is due, no prior at all counts as settled; with neither, due when the asker can ask the row, `LlmAsker.can_ask`: an abstract or excerpt, or a title under `title_basis`). So the first run on this code asks every document never asked under the current digest, and a new prompt name, model or template (question digest and asker name move; every row is in scope by `in_scope` anyway) re-asks every document. **Order and completeness**: the stage hands the asker the question scope's rows first, then the rest, each in `doc_id` order (the asker admits rows in the order given), so a budget or `max_rows` stop cuts signals before any answer that decides; a signal pair left `not_attempted` does not make the run incomplete (count `signal_not_attempted`; the next run finds it due), so the signal backlog never holds a build or a release back. Counts `signal_pairs` (requested pairs outside the question scope), `signals` (stored with a verdict). **Rules kept**: every gate rule stays a decision rule (batch-2026-10a: `newsletter_posts`, `manual_accept`, `selected_links`, `frontier_lab_posts`, `safety_org_posts`, `zvi_posts`, and the `sql:` fetch of `url` rows with no abstract and no excerpt): arm 1, origin `rule`, unchanged; none stands in for the verdict any more, since their rows are asked too. What stood in and is gone: the question scope as the asking scope (both exclusions) and D697's settling under an asker. No call remains only for a row with no abstract, no excerpt and no title (`skipped[no_basis]` fill, not due; 30 rows on the head). **No format change**: the signal uses `QUESTION`'s existing fields; code before D724 reads a signal as the plain fill (it ignores the verdict), so rolling back is safe. Digests: none move (plan, gate, triage `config_digest`, question digests of every plan in `configs/plans/` compared before and after: identical; batch-2026-10a plan a9a43bf0…, triage config 8a4c4ba0…); the code digest does. On the head of ws1qpn8myzxah (read-only simulation with the stage's gate functions): 65,417 rows due (60,492 with a primary role `ok`, 4,925 `rule`/`sql:` fetch; all outside the question scope; 60,449 with an older-prompt verdict in evidence, none with current-digest evidence), 0 in `in_scope` or `question_due`; their decisions recompute unchanged (arm 7 60,485, arm 1 4,925, arm 6 7; 0 mismatches); estimated $9.5-11 (openai/gpt-6-luna via OpenRouter, mean $0.000154 per fields call, $0.000107 per title call, from the current prompts' evidence), about 20 min at 256 workers, within the line's $20. | D731 (verify-cache) | **A verify and a build parse each parquet footer once: `stack.store.parquet.read_footer` / `read_raw` and a `footer_cache` block around `run_checks` and the whole of `run_build`, keyed by the footer's bytes (amends D280's per-check reads; no check, message, order or exit code changes).** (1) Every footer read of the checks, the chain resolver (`_read_chain_file`, `_check_ids`) and the family reader (`read_family`, `read_family_fields`, `file_format`) goes through `read_footer` (schema, header, row count; `schema_digest` computed on first use), every raw data read through `read_raw` (`pq.ParquetFile(path, metadata=...).read(columns)`, which drops `pq.read_table`'s dataset discovery and its second footer parse; one chunk per column instead of one per row group and 128Ki rows, the values the same; an unknown or repeated column raises `ValueError` where `ParquetFile.read` would ignore it). (2) Inside a block the cache key is `(file size, sha256 of the footer bytes and trailer)`, read from the file afresh on every lookup (one tail read, up to a few hundred KB): a file changed or replaced within the block, also with its size, mtime and inode kept, is a miss and reads as it now is; everything cached is a function of those bytes, so a hit returns what an uncached parse would. A miss is kept only when the key is the same after the parse as before it and the schema reads; a footer that does not read is not cached and raises as before. Data pages are never cached. Nothing outlives the block (a contextvar; a nested block shares the outer one). (3) Memory: schemas, headers and digests for every distinct footer (about 55 MB for all 693 files of the production store), parsed `FileMetaData` (about 0.5 MB each there) only for the 64 newest (`METADATA_ENTRIES`); caching all of them measured +371 MB. Measured at `-n 2` on the shared box, base a6a74e9 vs this branch, interleaved: one full verify on the clean 10-file fixture store 6.13 s → 3.50 s (footer parses 290 → 10, `schema_digest` 242 → 10), structural 0.30 → 0.12 s, a build's finish parts 1.34 → 0.82 s; fast tier 179.2 → 150.6 s; slow tier 1069.7 → 773.5 s; full suite 1223.2 → 912.4 s (`3819` → `3833 passed, 6 skipped`). A copy of the release store export (46 files, 1.3 GB): structural 24.5 → 23.5 s, files+build_set 570.6 → 568.8 s, identical results: on real data the reads, not the footers, are the cost. Tests: `tests/test_store_parquet.py` (one parse per footer inside a block, none kept outside or after it, the metadata bound, an in-place change read as it now is, an unreadable footer raising alike, `read_raw` = `pq.read_table`), `tests/test_verify_modes.py` (a verify parses each footer and computes each digest once; a footer changed between verifies, and within one block, is found with the results of an uncached verify); red with a key of path/size/mtime/inode, with a cache that outlives its block, and with no cache. | impl/120 verify-cache |
| D732 (duckdb-tmp) | **Every duckdb connection of the pipeline is opened by `stack.duck.connect()`, which sets `temp_directory` to `<$STACK_TMP, else tempfile.gettempdir()>/duckdb-<pid>-<random>`; the image's dataset export also needs `jsonschema`, now a base dependency.** (1) Cause: duckdb's default `temp_directory` for an in-memory database is `.tmp` relative to the working directory, created on the first spill past `memory_limit`; in the image the working directory `/app` is root-owned and the cycle runs as `stack` (uid 1000). The 2026-10-27 Railway test cycle (code 3f76c13) built `ok`, then `stack export --config dataset-public` failed in `observed_values` with `IOException: IO Error: Failed to create directory ".tmp": Permission denied`. Local runs never hit it (writable checkouts; the directory is removed on close). (2) The spill directory is named, not created: duckdb creates it on a spill and removes it on close, so no two connections share one and a run without a spill leaves nothing; a relative or unwritable base is refused when the connection opens. `external_access=False` (`stack.query.sql_connection`) SETs `enable_external_access = false` right after the connection opens: duckdb refuses `temp_directory` in the same `config` as it. Memory and thread limits stay at the call sites. All 11 `duckdb.connect` sites (`stack/dashdata.py`, `stack/checks/blocks.py`, `stack/query.py`, `stack/cli/show.py` x2, `stack/store/chain.py`, `stack/evals/release_quality.py`, `stack/fold/dataset.py` x3, `workflows/gather/normalise.py`; `tools/` had none) use it; `tests/test_duck.py` refuses `duckdb.connect` and duckdb's module-level default-connection calls elsewhere under `stack/`, `tools/`, `workflows/` (the frozen scripts under `evals/` and the tests keep plain connections: they run on writable checkouts). (3) Image: `TMPDIR=/work/scratch` (already set) is the spill base; `HF_HOME=/work/cache/huggingface` explicit; every write goes under `/work`. (4) With (1) fixed, the export in the image failed next on `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'jsonschema'` (the bundle checks; a dev-group package, the image installs `--no-dev`): `jsonschema>=4.21` moves to the project dependencies (uv.lock: no pin moves); `tests/test_scheduled_run.py` checks that every third-party module imported under `stack/`, `workflows/` and by `tools/scheduled_run.py` is in the image's install closure (Dockerfile groups through uv.lock) unless listed optional (docling, polars, playwright, referencing). (5) Verified in podman, as the image's user, `--read-only` root, `--network=none`, a writable `/work`, on a copy of the release store export (build ws1qpn8myzxah): the base image (e5cdae6) fails at `dataset.py:1715 in observed_values` with the production message (`Permission denied` with a writable root, `Read-only file system` with `--read-only`); this branch's image writes the public bundle (39,269 rows, 3.5 min; a 1.1 GB spill directory under `/work/scratch`, gone at the end), byte-identical to a local run of the same commit except the timestamp and code-commit stamp in README.md/release.json. | D733 (acquire-tail) | **A build short only on acquire's retry tail (reasons `halted`, `time`, `pending`; collector lines may be short too) is releasable by the scheduled cycle, a WARN naming the tail; after one that ended `halted` the cycle runs no further build; and within a build a run that ended `halted` with fewer than 10 items ok ends its line's `repeat`.** Why: the 2026-10-27 Railway test cycle's build wtwv0wpnr8hfv spent 217 min and ended `incomplete: acquire (halted)`: acquire runs 1-2 ended on the clock / `pending` (26 and 12 roles ok), runs 3-6 `halted` (the OA lane's lane-wide 429 on Unpaywall or the ID Converter, `halt_run`) with 0, 0, 1 and 3 roles ok over ~85 min, on a ~677-row retry tail; the cycle then had no releasable build (exit 3, ERROR), and in production every later build of the cycle would repeat the same halted acquire and no cycle would release while the 429s last. (1) `stack/build.py` `halt_ends_repeat` / `HALTED_REPEAT_MIN_OK = 10`: a run whose reasons (`incomplete_reasons`) include `halted` and whose `counts["outcome.ok"]` is below 10 ends the repeat (a build note names the run and its `halted.<lane>` lanes); the build goes on, verifies and ends `incomplete` as before. General, not OA-specific: the halt reason is the skeleton's (any acquire lane), annotate's fatal LLM error and a collector halt use it too; a stage without `outcome.ok` counts 0. A halted run that still completed 10 or more (another lane cut short by the clock, a late halt) is repeated as before: skipping only the halted lane in follow-up runs would need a lane exclusion the skeleton does not have. Threshold from the record: 26 and 12 before the halt, 0-3 after. In the incident the repeat now stops after run 3 (saves runs 4-6, ~80 min). (2) `tools/scheduled_run.py`: `ACQUIRE_TAIL = {halted, time, pending}`; `classify_build` returns the new verdict `tail` when acquire is the only `NEEDS_BUILD` line short and its reasons are a non-empty subset of it (`TOLERATED["acquire"]` gains `halted`, so it is no longer an "unexpected" WARN); acquire short for `limit`, `not_run` or `unspecified`, or triage/annotate short, stays `again`. On `tail` with `halted` the builds stop (the tail is rate-limited by a provider; a later build within hours is likely to meet the same 429s); on `time`/`pending` alone the next build goes on while acquire wrote rows (a catch-up; 0 rows ends the builds instead of halting the cycle), and the newest `tail` build is released when no build ends `ok`. The release: WARN `build … short only on acquire's retry tail (<reasons>; last acquire run <id>: <scope.due> rows due, <outcome.failed_transient> roles failed_transient, <refresh_pending> waiting on a retry_after, halted lanes: …; <n> roles ok over the build's <k> acquire runs); released, the next cycle retries the tail`; outcome `ok`, exit 0, then the usual export (`--allow-incomplete`, as for the `collectors` case), staging and upload. Not released after a stop (the watchdog cancels a child past the drain grace) nor with `STACK_SCHED_RELEASE_ALLOW_INCOMPLETE=0`; a later `failed` build still halts the cycle without a release. Why such a build is a correct release (read, not run on the store): both folds of the plan filter `has_text`, so the tail's documents (no current ok text) are not in the corpus and every later line (screen, affiliation, technique_staged, model_roles, fold.build) ran complete on what is; `release.json` `build_status` carries `incomplete` with the acquire entry (D705); a document fetched in a later cycle gets a new text digest, so the annotate lines ask it as new. Not done: per-document backoff across cycles (roles already carry the provider's `retry_after`, counted `refresh_pending`; a cross-cycle schedule is a separate change). Plan digest unchanged (a9a43bf0…). Tests: `tests/test_scenario_m5.py::test_a_halted_acquire_run_ends_the_repeat_unless_it_made_progress` (the synthetic acquire gains `halt_from`/`halted_ok`; red with the rule off: 6 runs, not 2); `tests/test_scheduled_run.py::test_classify_build` (the `acquire (time, pending)` and `acquire (time) + gather (limit)` cases now expect `tail`, per the rule, plus six new cases), `::test_a_build_short_only_on_acquires_halted_tail_is_released_and_ends_the_builds` (the incident's records: one build 2.x, both exports `--allow-incomplete`, uploaded, one WARN), `::test_an_acquire_tail_on_the_clock_goes_on_and_the_newest_tail_build_is_released` (also: a tail build then one short on triage releases the tail build; release-incomplete off ends exit 3); red without the halted stop and without the verdict. Docs: `v4/DEPLOY-railway.md` steps 4-5 and the severity table, `v4/OPERATE.md` (acquire's clocks), `configs/plans/README.md` (`repeat`). | Tomáš 2026-10-28 (release a build short only on acquire's retry tail; stop repeating acquire after a halted run) |

Appended rather than edited: the store is append-only and the original stays the record of the paid call; a re-keyed row is told apart by its run (stage record, build note) and its pointer. Build `whrrcdb93tr06` (1,670 s) re-keyed 39,269 rows per stage (technique_staged ok 33,254, empty 6,004, failed_permanent 11; model_roles 29,358 / 9,901 / 10; each row's result digest checked in the run), 0 requests; `stack verify --build` on it: 43 checks ok, 4 skipped (structural; V7, V8, X6, X7, X8 ok). (1) **Plan**: an `annotate.<wf>` line of an evidence-keeping workflow, and the `triage` line per gate question, may carry `target` (the config digest its pin gives; triage `{question: digest}`) and `accepted: [{config, name, decision, note?, question?}]` in preference order. Both are in the plan digest and in no line digest, so the config digest stays the identity of what produces an answer (editing the list orphans nothing). Refused at load: another stage, malformed digests, `accepted` without `target` or the reverse, the target in the list, a config twice, a question the gate does not ask. The build refuses at its start (`--dry-run`: under `preflight`) a `target` the pin no longer gives, so a later pin change does not inherit the list unseen. (2) **Stage start** (before any call): each accepted config is one the stage recorded with the same `workflow`, `registry_version` and `produced` as the current pin (annotate: a run record's `prompt_pin`; triage: prior `triage_evidence`) and `name` matches it (annotate: the prompt name plus `@<tag>` of each vendored vocabulary the pin carries, `stack.annotate.stage.config_name`, e.g. `technique-staged-v5-a1.1@techniques-1.0.0`; triage: a prompt name of that evidence). (3) **Selection**: the target's decided answer wins, else the first accepted config with a decided answer for the same source and basis; failures are never accepted, a basis change is never crossed, nothing is copied or relabelled; annotate ask and select and every produced record use one lookup, triage carries accepted `ok` answers and signals under their own digest as final and settled. Counted `carried.accepted`. No re-judge scope (dropped with `class`, ids and the snapshot blob). (4) **Selection digest**: sha256 of the JCS of `{target, accepted}` per stage (`stack.plan.selection_digest`), in each annotate and triage run record's `selection` (`{digest, target, accepted}`), in `release.json` `stages` and in `tools/list_configs.py` (read-only: a stage's recorded configs with their names, rows and the line's selection digest); it names which set of answers a stage ships. (5) **Checks**: X8 reselects with the run's recorded selection; X6 requires a selected row of another config to be in it and judges an `ai_check` one against its own run's pin; both check the selection's target and digest. (6) **Release**: `release.json` `stages`: per annotate stage of the build `selection_digest`, `target` and `accepted`, each `{config, name, config_id, documents}` (the build's selection copied: the release config does not choose configs); FORMAT.md one sentence per accepted config. model_roles' vocabulary is found by the sha256 its pin names among `taxonomy/models-{1.0.0,1.1.0}.yaml` (new vendored symlinks), one taxonomy file per (name, version) ships (the build's own configs' too), two sha256 for one name and version are refused, `release.json` `taxonomies` lists versions per name (`stack/dashdata.py` reads the newest), and `parameters.role` is the run's recorded `prompt_pin.role_params` (null with a note for runs before this), never today's `llm.yaml`. A not_attempted row of an LLM workflow no longer breaks the export. (7) **Rehearsal** (a hard-link copy of the impl/126 store copy, no key, a refusing transport, caps $0.01): build `wyyw9t9manvw0` (1,384 s) ended `incomplete`: technique_staged kept 39,258 accepted answers and model_roles 39,259, the 11 + 10 documents without a decided 1.0.0 answer were cut by the caps (`not_attempted[budget]`), 0 LLM calls and 0 transport requests; affiliation_orgs recomputed 42,437 documents. `stack verify --build`: 43 ok, 4 skipped (structural). Both exports (`--allow-incomplete`, 39,269 rows) equal impl/126's round-2 exports column for column, the technique and model kinds row for row (1.0.0 `config_id`s and taxonomy version); they differ in affiliation_orgs `config_id` / `decided_at` (24,755, recomputed), 10 model_name_matches rows (a cap artefact) and the bundled techniques-1.1.0 and models-1.1.0 files beside the 1.0.0 ones. (8) **Not done**: affiliation_orgs is not accepted (its round-2 config pinned orgs-0.2.0 bytes that D738 changed under the same version, so its file could not ship beside the current one; it recomputes without calls); the gleaning replay fix (D738). Revision 10's plan digest: `415b9dfcdca23a1544dc542c8accb79df9636f002de09cb8f2ad82f6385fc56c`. | D769 (acquire-rules) | **A build short only on acquire's retry tail (D733's `tail` verdict) is released also when a cap or stop comes after it, before or during the catch-up build; and it is released only while the tail is at most `STACK_SCHED_TAIL_MAX_PCT` (default 5) percent of the documents acquire covers: the last acquire run's `counts["scope.due"]` over its `counts["scope.fetch"]` (amends D733, D734).** Why: impl/140 found two behaviours D733 left: (a) a clock tail with progress, then the wall or USD cap before the catch-up build, ended `stopped`, exit 3, ERROR with no release, although the tail build is as releasable as after a halted acquire (its corpus is written, every line after acquire ran complete on it, and a stop changes neither); (b) "retry tail" was unbounded: acquire short on its clock with a fresh backlog of 20,000 due rows was released as a tail (WARN, exit 0) on every build. (1) `tools/scheduled_run.py` `steps_all`: the newest tail build is released (WARN `… released after the cycle stopped (<reason>), the next cycle retries the tail`, exit 0) whatever stopped the cycle: the wall or USD cap, `hold.json`, a signal, a lost lock (`Children.request_stop` is the one path; the approval named it). D733 kept the release out after a stop because the watchdog would cut it: the watchdog's cap check asked for the stop again every `watch_s` (600 s) and each request sent the running child another SIGTERM (so a capped build was cancelled after ~10 min, not the documented 30), and its exit came 2 x the drain grace after the stop whatever child was running then. Now `request_stop` signals only on the first request (the cancel is the watchdog's, after the drain grace, as `v4/DEPLOY-railway.md` says), and a child started after the stop (only the release's exports are) restarts the watchdog's clock: it is never signalled and has 2 x the drain grace (60 min) from its own start before the exit (exports measured 350 s public, 465 s internal, 701 s internal from a cold mirror). A build that ends `ok` and a stop that comes during its export: unchanged (the export gets the first SIGTERM). (2) `Settings.tail_max_pct` (`STACK_SCHED_TAIL_MAX_PCT`, a percentage 0-100, default 5; the name avoids the `_LIMIT`/`_FRACTION` endings the preflight refuses), `tail_share`, `tail_words`: the tail is the last acquire run's `scope.due` (documents with a fetch role due and fetchable when that run started: `not_attempted`, or `retry_after` passed; `workflows/acquire/scope.py`), so at most what that run left; the base is that run's `scope.fetch` (documents in acquire's scope that triage lets it fetch, fetched already or not). "The documents due" of the approval is read as that base, not as `scope.due` itself: the tail is most of the due rows by construction (the incident's last run: 677 due, 3 ok). Released while `due * 100 <= pct * covered`; above it, or with either count missing (or `scope.fetch` 0), no release: ERROR `no releasable build (build … short on acquire's retry tail over its limit: <due> rows due, <p>% of the <covered> rows acquire covers …)`, exit 3, as before D733. The limit decides the release only; whether another build runs is D733/D734's rule as before. (2) **Measured** (fake model, `annotate.screen`, threads by `/proc/self/status`): the pool's threads are `min(rows, workers)` above the process's base and return to it when the run ends (base 25: 64 workers 90 at 100 and at 400 rows; 256 workers 238 at 400 rows); nothing in the ask path starts threads per call (`stack.llm`'s transport is `urllib`), so the thread count is bounded by `workers` and this was the container's limit, not a leak. A pool on the fallback has taken the container's last free tasks and holds them until it ends (a pool's threads end only at its shutdown), so another thread or process started meanwhile can fail too; where the limit is enforced but cannot be read (a parent cgroup's `pids.max` while the container's own shows `max`), the operator's ceiling `STACK_POOL_MAX_THREADS` (a positive integer, unset = none; read when a pool is made, in no digest; the scheduler's build child inherits it and its preflight refuses a malformed value) caps every pool first. | D789 (s3-slowdown) | **A blob's S3 upload is repeated after a transient failure (`SlowDown`, a 5xx, a connection error: `is_s3_transient`) after each of `stack.store.blobs.UPLOAD_RETRY_DELAYS` = 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 120 s, each scaled by a random factor in [0.5, 1.5) (about 4 min in all), in both the run's deferred uploader and the synchronous `put`; and a failed OpenAlex re-sweep in the scheduled cycle is a WARN and the cycle goes on, where it halted.** (1) **Cause**: the first production cycle 20261101T2240Z-c025 (code 39b6ad69) began with the due re-sweep (`collect.openalex`, `STACK_OPENALEX_FULL=1`, run `r048fcy6z4vng`); it completed all 152 queries (2,822 pages, 549,063 works fetched, 79,403 provider records minted as blobs, 1.45 GB) and then ended `failed[s3_transient]` with no outputs after 110.1 min: `BlobStore.flush` raised the first upload error its workers had kept, a `put_object` of a blob answered `SlowDown` past the client's own retries. Those are botocore's standard mode with `max_attempts` 4 (`S3Config.client`): three repeats after at most 1, 2 and 4 s (`rand * 2^n`), and none at all once the client's retry quota (500, 5 per throttled repeat, shared by the run's 16 upload workers) is spent in a burst. The blob upload was the one S3 write of a run with no repeat of its own (the publish's data PUT has `DATA_PUT_RETRY_DELAYS`, S25-47; downloads `DOWNLOAD_RETRY_S`), and its failure, whenever it happened in the run, surfaced only at the flush before the publish. D786 (the upload-thread start) changed neither concurrency (16 workers, `max_pool_connections` 32) nor retries. The scheduler then halted on the re-sweep's rc (cycle spend $2.02, the run's OpenAlex cost; the prepaid balance fell $1.14), so no build ran. (2) **Repeat**: the HEAD-then-PUT of one blob is the repeated unit (a blob is immutable under its digest, so a repeat is safe); a non-transient failure, the last repeat, or a failure after the store was closed (a cancelled or failed run) raises as before (`failed[s3_transient]`). The first repeat and every power-of-two-th of a store's repeats are said on stderr (`warning: blob <digest> upload failed (ClientError[SlowDown]); retrying in …`). Jitter, so the workers a throttle hits together do not return together; per worker, not a shared pause. The client config is unchanged (no adaptive mode: its rate limiter would pace every S3 call of the process, the job ticks included); job ticks keep their own failure rule (D354, D493), with no repeat added inside a tick. (3) **The halt**: the re-sweep is a collector run beside the builds' own `collect.openalex` (the week's incremental pass, 60 days below each watermark, D582); its loss leaves only the works indexed later than that look-back for another week. A build short only on collector lines is released with a WARN (Tomáš 2026-10-26), so a failed re-sweep is a WARN the same way: `OpenAlex re-sweep failed (run <id> <status>[<class>], rc=<n>): the cycle goes on …`. A failed re-sweep publishes no `ok` `full_resweep` run, so `last_openalex_full` leaves it due and the next cycle repeats it. A failure that is not the re-sweep's own (a code bug, an exhausted OpenAlex budget) meets the builds' `collect.openalex` too and halts there; an OpenAlex budget stop stays ERROR (`openalex_budget_stops`). The standalone S2 collect, arXiv sweep and s2-lookup still halt on failure (not changed here). (4) **Not resumable**: a run publishes nothing before its end (D407: blobs, data, record), so a re-sweep that fails at its flush loses its pages: the next one pays the ~110 min and ~$1.1-2.0 of OpenAlex again; the blobs that did reach S3 are found by HEAD and not PUT again. Resuming would need a run that publishes per query (coverage windows and sources rows) or a re-sweep marker that lets a later run skip queries already re-swept since a given time; neither exists. (5) **Digests**: none moves (plan, config); the code digest moves as with any code change. (2) **Lookup** (`stack.evals.freeze.find_text`): a set's own `texts/<item_id>.txt.gz` (a fresh freeze, a test's edited copy) first, then the cache `<root>/<task>/<set_id>/<item_id>.txt.gz`, the key from the set's `manifest.json` (`task`, `set_id`), else its directory names; `<root>` is `$STACK_EVAL_TEXTS_DIR`, else `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/stack/eval-texts`, else `~/.cache/stack/eval-texts`. `stack.evals.harness.read_frozen_text` (every adapter's whole text) and the sets' own freeze/derive scripts (technique_staged 17a, 17b, 18a, 18b, 18c; model_roles 17a; technique_roles 13a) read through it; a missing text is an `EvalError` naming both places and the fetch command, raised by the input check before any call. (4) **The tool** `tools/fetch_eval_texts.py`: read-only (the store client with the read-only guard, GET only); the bucket from `--store`, `$STACK_STORE` or `$STACK_S3_BASE_URI` (environment, else `$STACK_ENV_FILE`), never written in the repository; the source is the `evals/` archive taken before the removal (`archived/2026-10-31-pipeline-evals-at-38330fc5/evals.tar.zst`, a key from the bucket root, `--archive` overrides), checked against its `SHA256SUMS`; a text is written only when its item is in the checkout and the sha256 of the text equals the item's `input.full_text_digest` (13-t2pool: the top-level `text_digest`); `--check` verifies a cache offline; `--from-tar` reads a local copy. Verified on 2026-11-01: 728 of 728 texts fetched and checked, byte-identical to the removed files. (5) The history still holds the texts until the history rewrite drops them. | 2026-11-01 decision to publish the repository |
